2026-11-12.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Josaphat Kuntsevych by Józef Simmler, about 1861. The archbishop was killed by a mob at Vitebsk in 1623. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.
2026-11-12.b: A Ukrainian Greek Catholic archbishop of Polotsk who worked for unity between Eastern Christians and Rome, and was martyred for it.

2026-11-13.a: Mother Cabrini around 1900. She crossed the Atlantic more than twenty times and founded sixty-seven schools, orphanages and hospitals; she was the first U.S. citizen to be canonized.
2026-11-13.b: An Italian missionary who founded schools, orphanages and hospitals for immigrants in the Americas. The first U.S. citizen to be canonized, she is patron of immigrants.

2026-11-14.a: The Unjust Judge, a wood engraving after John Everett Millais from The Parables of Our Lord, 1864. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2026-11-14.b: “Will not God vindicate his elect, who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long over them?”
2026-11-14.t: Saturday of the thirty-second week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-15.a: The Parable of the Talents by Willem de Poorter, a pupil of Rembrandt, about 1640s. A servant counts out his master's money by lamplight in a dark counting room.
2026-11-15.b: “Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your master.”

2026-11-16.a: Queen Saint Margaret of Scotland by Nicolas de Largillière, 1692, one of the leading portrait painters of Louis XIV's France. It hangs at Sizergh Castle in Cumbria, a National Trust house.
2026-11-16.b: An English princess who became Queen of Scotland. She reformed the Church there, founded abbeys and served the poor at her own table.

o.a: Queen Saint Margaret of Scotland by Nicolas de Largillière, 1692, one of the leading portrait painters of Louis XIV's France. It hangs at Sizergh Castle in Cumbria, a National Trust house.
o.b: An English princess who became Queen of Scotland. She reformed the Church there, founded abbeys and served the poor at her own table.

o.a: Saint Gertrude by Miguel Cabrera, 1763, the leading painter of colonial Mexico. Gertrude was hugely popular in New Spain; the Christ Child appears in her heart. It is in the Dallas Museum of Art.
o.b: A Benedictine nun of Helfta whose visions and writings helped spread devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

w.a: Christ Healing the Blind of Jericho by Nicolas Poussin, 1650. On the road outside the city, Christ touches the eyes of one blind man while the other gropes his way forward. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
w.b: “Receive your sight; your faith has made you well.”
w.t: Monday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-17.a: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary by Simone Martini, about 1317–20, among the saints he painted in the Lower Church of San Francesco, Assisi. She died less than a century before, and the Franciscans already counted her as one of their own.
2026-11-17.b: A Hungarian princess and widow who gave her wealth to the poor and built a hospital at Marburg. She died at twenty-four and is patron of Franciscan tertiaries and charities.

2026-11-18.a: St. Peter's, Rome, by Viviano Codazzi, about 1630. Michelangelo's dome had been finished only a few decades earlier. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2026-11-18.b: A feast of the two great Roman basilicas raised over the tombs of the apostles: St. Peter's on the Vatican Hill and St. Paul's Outside the Walls.

o.a: St. Peter's, Rome, by Viviano Codazzi, about 1630. Michelangelo's dome had been finished only a few decades earlier. It is in the Museo del Prado.
o.b: A feast of the two great Roman basilicas raised over the tombs of the apostles: St. Peter's on the Vatican Hill and St. Paul's Outside the Walls.
o.t: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul, Apostles

o.a: Rose Philippine Duchesne, who founded the first house of the Society of the Sacred Heart in America in 1818. At seventy-one she went to live among the Potawatomi, who called her 'woman who prays always.'
o.b: A French Religious of the Sacred Heart who brought her order to Missouri, opening schools on the frontier. The Potawatomi called her 'Woman Who Prays Always.'

2026-11-18.t: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul, Apostles

w.a: The Return of the Lord, from a series of six engravings on the parable of the talents made in 1565 by Harmen Jansz. Muller after Maarten van Heemskerck. The master comes home to settle accounts with his servants. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
w.b: “Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.”
w.by: Harmen Jansz. Muller after Maarten van Heemskerck
w.t: Wednesday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-19.a: Flevit super illam ('He Wept over It') by Enrique Simonet, 1892. From the Mount of Olives, Christ weeps as he looks across at the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the Museo del Prado collection, on loan to the Museum of Málaga.
2026-11-19.b: “Would that even today you knew the things that make for peace! But now they are hid from your eyes.”
2026-11-19.t: Thursday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-20.a: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple, a Dutch print after a design by Jacob Jordaens, made between 1652 and 1702. Christ raises a whip of cords as the traders flee and the cattle stampede. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2026-11-20.b: “It is written, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.”
2026-11-20.t: Friday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-21.a: The Presentation of the Virgin by Titian, 1534–38. The little girl climbs the Temple steps alone, watched by a crowd of Venetians. It still hangs in the room it was painted for, the Sala dell'Albergo of the old Scuola della Carità, now part of the Accademia Galleries, Venice.
2026-11-21.b: According to an ancient tradition, Mary as a little girl was brought by her parents to the Temple in Jerusalem and dedicated to God.
2026-11-21.t: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2026-11-22.a: Christ Pantocrator, 'ruler of all', by Angelos Akotantos, the leading Cretan icon painter of the early 1400s. Christ blesses with one hand and holds the Gospel in the other.
2026-11-22.b: The last Sunday of the Church's year proclaims Christ as King of all creation, whose kingdom is 'of truth and life, of holiness and grace, of justice, love and peace.'
2026-11-22.t: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe

2026-11-23.a: Father Miguel Pro on the day of his arrest in 1927, in the civilian clothes he wore to minister in secret. The government photographed his execution to deter others; instead the pictures made him a hero.
2026-11-23.b: A Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during the persecution of the Church. Executed by firing squad, he died with arms outstretched, crying 'Viva Cristo Rey!'

o.a: Saint Clement Striking the Rock by Bernardino Fungai, about 1500. Exiled to the Crimean mines, legend says, Clement saw a lamb on a hill and struck the rock there, and water gushed out for the thirsty prisoners. It is in the York Art Gallery.
o.b: The fourth Bishop of Rome, who may have known Peter and Paul. His letter to the quarreling church at Corinth is one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament.
o.t: Saint Clement I, Pope and Martyr

o.a: A fresco in the hermitage of San Colombano at Trambileno, Trentino, a tiny chapel built into a cliff face above a gorge. It is one of many places across Europe named for the wandering Irish monk.
o.b: An Irish monk who founded monasteries across France and Italy, from Luxeuil to Bobbio, carrying Irish learning to the continent.

o.a: Father Miguel Pro on the day of his arrest in 1927, in the civilian clothes he wore to minister in secret. The government photographed his execution to deter others; instead the pictures made him a hero.
o.b: A Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during the persecution of the Church. Executed by firing squad, he died with arms outstretched, crying 'Viva Cristo Rey!'
o.t: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro, Priest and Martyr

2026-11-23.t: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro, Priest and Martyr

w.a: The Widow's Mite by the French painter Émile Auguste Hublin (1830–1891). A poor widow drops her two small coins into the Temple treasury. It is in the Herbert Art Gallery and Museum, Coventry.
w.b: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.”
w.t: Monday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-24.a: A Vietnamese painting from the mid-1800s showing the execution of Paul Mi, Peter Duong and Peter Truat on December 18, 1838. Pictures like this were made at the time to record the martyrs, and some were carried back to Paris by missionaries.
2026-11-24.b: A Vietnamese priest who gave his life with 116 companions—priests, catechists and lay people—during waves of persecution in Vietnam. They were canonized together in 1988.
2026-11-24.t: Saint Andrew Dũng-Lạc, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

2026-11-25.a: Saint Catherine of Alexandria by Caravaggio, about 1598, painted for his patron Cardinal del Monte. She kneels beside the broken spiked wheel, a sword in her hand. His model was a Roman courtesan, Fillide Melandroni. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
2026-11-25.b: According to legend, a learned young noblewoman of Alexandria who out-argued the emperor's philosophers and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered, she was beheaded.

o.a: Saint Catherine of Alexandria by Caravaggio, about 1598, painted for his patron Cardinal del Monte. She kneels beside the broken spiked wheel, a sword in her hand. His model was a Roman courtesan, Fillide Melandroni. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
o.b: According to legend, a learned young noblewoman of Alexandria who out-argued the emperor's philosophers and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered, she was beheaded.
o.t: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Virgin and Martyr

2026-11-25.t: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Virgin and Martyr

w.a: The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer by Jean-Léon Gérôme, commissioned in 1863 and finished twenty years later. In a Roman arena a group of Christians kneel together in prayer as a lion steps out of its cage. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
w.b: “But not a hair of your head will perish. By your endurance you will gain your lives.”
w.t: Wednesday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-26.a: Thanksgiving at Plymouth by Jennie Augusta Brownscombe, 1925, her second version of a scene she first painted in 1914. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington.
2026-11-26.b: A national day of gratitude to God for the harvest and the blessings of the year, kept on the fourth Thursday of November.

o.a: Thanksgiving at Plymouth by Jennie Augusta Brownscombe, 1925, her second version of a scene she first painted in 1914. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington.
o.b: A national day of gratitude to God for the harvest and the blessings of the year, kept on the fourth Thursday of November.

w.a: The Destruction of the Temple of Jerusalem by Francesco Hayez, 1867. Roman soldiers storm the Temple in AD 70 as the city burns, the fall Jesus foretold. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
w.b: “And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.”
w.t: Thursday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-27.a: The Great Day of His Wrath by John Martin, 1851–53, the first of three vast paintings of the Last Judgment. Mountains collapse and a city tumbles into the abyss — 'heaven and earth will pass away.' It is in Tate Britain, London.
2026-11-27.b: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.”
2026-11-27.t: Friday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-28.a: The Last Judgment by Rogier van der Weyden, 1445–50, painted for the hospital of Beaune in Burgundy so that the sick could see it from their beds. St. Michael weighs souls beneath Christ in judgment. It is still in the Hôtel-Dieu, Beaune.
2026-11-28.b: “But watch at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that will take place, and to stand before the Son of man.”
2026-11-28.t: Saturday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2026-11-29.a: The Wise and Foolish Virgins by William Blake, about 1822. At midnight the bridegroom's coming is announced by an angel with a trumpet; the wise virgins hold their lamps ready while the foolish beg for oil. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2026-11-29.b: “What I say to you I say to all: Watch.”

2026-11-30.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Andrew by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, painted in Seville around 1675–82. Andrew is bound to the X-shaped cross that became his emblem, as light breaks through the clouds above. It hangs in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.
2026-11-30.b: A fisherman of Galilee and brother of Peter, he was the first apostle Jesus called. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross in Greece; he is patron of Scotland.

2026-12-01.a: The Prophet Isaiah by Michelangelo, 1508–12, on the Sistine Chapel ceiling — one of the prophets who longed to see what the disciples saw. He turns from his book as if called by the angel at his shoulder.
2026-12-01.b: “Blessed are the eyes which see what you see! For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.”
2026-12-01.t: Tuesday of the first week of Advent

2026-12-02.a: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1670–74, painted for the church of the Hospital de la Caridad in Seville, a brotherhood that fed the poor. It still hangs there.
2026-12-02.b: “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have been with me now three days, and have nothing to eat; and I am unwilling to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the way.”
2026-12-02.t: Wednesday of the first week of Advent

2026-12-03.a: The famous Japanese portrait of Francis Xavier, painted in the early 1600s and found in 1920, hidden in the home of a family of secret Christians near Osaka. He gazes up at the cross, his heart aflame. It is in the Kobe City Museum.
2026-12-03.b: One of St. Ignatius's first companions, he sailed for Asia and preached the Gospel in India, Malaysia and Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China and is patron of missions.

2026-12-04.a: Saint John of Damascus in a 14th or 15th-century fresco on Mount Athos. He wears the turban he would have worn as an official at the Caliph's court in Damascus, before he became a monk.
2026-12-04.b: A monk near Jerusalem who defended the veneration of holy images during the iconoclast controversy. A Doctor of the Church.

o.a: Saint John of Damascus in a 14th or 15th-century fresco on Mount Athos. He wears the turban he would have worn as an official at the Caliph's court in Damascus, before he became a monk.
o.b: A monk near Jerusalem who defended the veneration of holy images during the iconoclast controversy. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint John Damascene, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2026-12-04.t: Saint John Damascene, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Italy before he settled in Spain. Christ touches the eyes of a kneeling blind man while the crowd argues around them. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
w.b: “According to your faith be it done to you.”
w.t: Friday of the first week of Advent

2026-12-05.a: The Harvesters by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1565, one of his series of the months. 'The harvest is abundant': peasants cut and stack golden wheat and rest at noon under a pear tree. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2026-12-05.b: “When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.”
2026-12-05.t: Saturday of the first week of Advent

2026-12-06.a: The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1566. A crowd of every kind of person gathers in a forest clearing to hear John, and among them, near the center, stands Christ. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.
2026-12-06.b: “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.”

2026-12-07.a: A detail of the polyptych of Saint Ambrose by Giovanni Barbagelata, 1499, still in the parish church of Sant'Ambrogio in Varazze on the Ligurian coast. Ambrose is shown in bishop's robes, with the scourge he used against heresy.
2026-12-07.b: A Roman governor who was acclaimed Bishop of Milan by the people before he was even baptized. A great preacher and hymn-writer, he stood up to emperors and baptized St. Augustine.
2026-12-07.t: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2026-12-08.a: The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1678. Looted from Seville by Napoleon's Marshal Soult, it was bought by the Louvre in 1852 for the highest price ever paid for a painting, and returned to Spain in 1941. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2026-12-08.b: The Church celebrates that Mary, by a singular grace, was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Patronal feast of the United States.
2026-12-08.t: The Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2026-12-09.a: Saint Juan Diego with the Tilma, a Mexican painting of 1737. He opens his cloak to show the roses he gathered in December, and the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on the cloth.
2026-12-09.b: An Indigenous Mexican to whom the Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak: Our Lady of Guadalupe.

o.a: Saint Juan Diego with the Tilma, a Mexican painting of 1737. He opens his cloak to show the roses he gathered in December, and the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on the cloth.
o.b: An Indigenous Mexican to whom the Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak: Our Lady of Guadalupe.

w.a: Christus Consolator ('Christ the Comforter') by Ary Scheffer, 1851. The weary, the grieving, the captive and the oppressed gather around Christ, who looks up to heaven.
w.b: “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”
w.t: Wednesday of the second week of Advent

2026-12-10.a: The Madonna of Loreto by Domenico Fiasella, about 1643. Angels carry the Holy House of Nazareth through the air to Loreto, as the legend tells. It is in the Diocesan Museum, Genoa.
2026-12-10.b: The Holy House of Loreto, venerated as the home of the Holy Family at Nazareth, has drawn pilgrims for centuries. Our Lady of Loreto is patron of aviators.

o.a: The Madonna of Loreto by Domenico Fiasella, about 1643. Angels carry the Holy House of Nazareth through the air to Loreto, as the legend tells. It is in the Diocesan Museum, Genoa.
o.b: The Holy House of Loreto, venerated as the home of the Holy Family at Nazareth, has drawn pilgrims for centuries. Our Lady of Loreto is patron of aviators.

w.a: Saint John the Baptist in the Wilderness by Caravaggio, about 1604. The prophet sits alone in the dark, wrapped in a red cloak, his reed cross beside him. It is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.
w.b: “Truly, I say to you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist.”
w.t: Thursday of the second week of Advent

2026-12-11.a: Saint Damasus, a 16th-century Portuguese panel by an unknown painter, in the Alberto Sampaio Museum in Guimarães—the city that claims him as a native son.
2026-12-11.b: Pope who commissioned St. Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin, the Vulgate. He honored the martyrs by restoring the catacombs and writing verses for their tombs.
