w.a: Children's Games by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1560. A whole town square is taken over by children playing some eighty different games, like the children in the market place Jesus describes. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
w.b: “We piped to you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.”
w.t: Friday of the second week of Advent

2026-12-12.a: The original image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on Juan Diego's cloak, from 1531. It hangs above the altar of the Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City, the most visited Marian shrine in the world, where visitors pass beneath it on a moving walkway.
2026-12-12.b: In 1531 the Virgin Mary appeared to St. Juan Diego at Tepeyac, near Mexico City, leaving her image on his cloak. She is patroness of the Americas.

2026-12-13.a: Saint John the Baptist Preaching by Paolo Veronese, about 1562. John points toward a distant figure — Christ, 'the one among you whom you do not recognize.' It is in the Galleria Borghese, Rome.
2026-12-13.b: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord.’”

2026-12-14.a: Christ Crucified with a Carmelite friar, probably John of the Cross, attributed to Agustín del Castillo, early 1600s. John's own small drawing of Christ on the cross, seen from above, later inspired Salvador Dalí. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts of Córdoba.
2026-12-14.b: A Carmelite friar who worked with St. Teresa of Ávila to reform the order. His poems, including The Dark Night, are among the treasures of Spanish literature. A Doctor of the Church.
2026-12-14.t: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2026-12-15.a: The Parable of the Two Sons in the Vineyard, an engraving by Georg Pencz, about 1535, from his series The Story of Christ. Pencz was a pupil of Albrecht Dürer in Nuremberg. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2026-12-15.b: “What do you think? A man had two sons; and he went to the first and said, ‘Son, go and work in the vineyard today.’”
2026-12-15.t: Tuesday of the third week of Advent

2026-12-16.a: Saint John the Baptist in Prison Visited by Two Disciples by Giovanni di Paolo, 1455–60, one of a series of panels on John's life. John sends his disciples through the barred window to ask, 'Are you the one who is to come?' It is in the Art Institute of Chicago.
2026-12-16.b: “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good news preached to them.”
2026-12-16.t: Wednesday of the third week of Advent

2026-12-17.a: The Tree of Jesse, about 1500, from the circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans in Haarlem. The kings of Israel sit in the branches of a tree growing from the sleeping Jesse, with the Virgin and Child at the top. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2026-12-17.b: “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.”
2026-12-17.by: Circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans

2026-12-18.a: The Dream of Saint Joseph by Georges de La Tour, about 1640. By the light of a single candle, a child-like angel touches the sleeping Joseph's arm. It is in the Museum of Arts, Nantes.
2026-12-18.b: “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.”

2026-12-19.a: The Angel Appearing to Zechariah by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1486–90, in the Tornabuoni Chapel of Santa Maria Novella, Florence. Ghirlandaio filled the Temple with portraits of the leading men of Florence.
2026-12-19.b: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer is heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.”

2026-12-20.a: The Annunciation by Fra Angelico, about 1426, painted for a convent in Fiesole. On the left, Adam and Eve are driven out of Eden; under the loggia, Gabriel greets the new Eve. It is in the Prado Museum, Madrid.
2026-12-20.b: “Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.”

2026-12-21.a: The Visitation by Rogier van der Weyden, about 1435–40. Mary and Elizabeth, both expecting, meet on a path in the Flemish countryside, each resting a hand on the other. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Leipzig.
2026-12-21.b: “Blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfilment of what was spoken to her from the Lord.”
2026-12-21.m: Commemoration of Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church

o.a: Saint Peter Canisius, an anonymous portrait. The Dutch Jesuit's catechisms went through hundreds of editions in his lifetime and he was called the second apostle of Germany.
o.b: A Dutch Jesuit whose catechisms renewed Catholic life in Germany after the Reformation. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2026-12-22.a: The Madonna of the Magnificat by Sandro Botticelli, about 1483. Mary writes the words of her song in a book held by angels, while the Child guides her hand. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
2026-12-22.b: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden. For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.”

2026-12-23.a: The Naming of John the Baptist by Fra Angelico, about 1435. Zechariah, still unable to speak, writes 'His name is John' while Elizabeth's household looks on. It is in the Museo di San Marco, Florence.
2026-12-23.b: “He asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, ‘His name is John.’ And they all marveled.”
2026-12-23.m: Commemoration of Saint John of Kanty, Priest

o.a: A Miracle of Saint John of Kanty by Taddeo Kuntze, about 1767. The Kraków professor was known for giving away his own clothes and food to the poor. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.
o.b: A professor at the University of Kraków, known for his learning and his great generosity to the poor.

2026-12-24.a: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds by Thomas Cole, 1833–34, founder of the Hudson River School. The angel's light breaks over a vast moonlit landscape. It is in the Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, Virginia.
2026-12-24.b: “Through the tender mercy of our God, when the day shall dawn upon us from on high to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

2026-12-25.a: The Adoration of the Child by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. All the light comes from the baby. Badly damaged by a car bomb outside the Uffizi in 1993, it was restored and hangs again in the Uffizi, Florence.
2026-12-25.b: Christmas: the Son of God is born of the Virgin Mary in a stable at Bethlehem and laid in a manger, while angels sing to shepherds in the fields.

2026-12-26.a: The Sermon of Saint Stephen by Vittore Carpaccio, 1514, painted for the confraternity of St. Stephen in Venice. Turbaned listeners sit in an imaginary Jerusalem. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2026-12-26.b: One of the first seven deacons, 'full of grace and power.' Stoned to death in Jerusalem, he prayed for his killers as a young man named Saul looked on.

2026-12-27.a: The Doni Tondo by Michelangelo, about 1506, his only finished panel painting. It was made for the wedding of Agnolo Doni in Florence. The Child passes between Mary and Joseph, with nude youths behind and the infant John the Baptist. It is in the Uffizi, still in its original carved frame.
2026-12-27.b: A feast of the home at Nazareth, where Jesus grew 'in wisdom and age and grace' with Mary and Joseph. It is kept in the octave of Christmas as a model for every family.
2026-12-27.t: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph

2026-12-28.a: The Massacre of the Innocents by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1638, one of two he painted of the subject. Mothers fight Herod's soldiers for their children as cherubs bring the martyrs' crowns from above. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.
2026-12-28.b: The little boys of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. They are honored as the first to die for him.

2026-12-29.a: Simeon's Song of Praise by Rembrandt, 1631. In a vast, dim temple one shaft of light falls on old Simeon holding the Child, with Mary and Joseph kneeling beside him. It is in the Mauritshuis, The Hague.
2026-12-29.b: “Lord, now let your servant depart in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to your people Israel.”
2026-12-29.m: Commemoration of Saint Thomas Becket, Bishop and Martyr

o.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Thomas Becket by Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre, 1748. The king's knights strike down the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral. It is in the church of Notre-Dame-de-la-Nativité de Bercy, Paris.
o.b: Archbishop of Canterbury and former chancellor to King Henry II, murdered in his cathedral for defending the freedom of the Church.
o.t: Saint Thomas Becket, Bishop and Martyr

2026-12-29.t: Fifth Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord

2026-12-30.a: An Old Woman Reading, probably the Prophetess Anna, by Rembrandt, 1631. Light falls on the old woman's hand resting on the page of Scripture. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2026-12-30.b: “Coming up at that very hour she gave thanks to God, and spoke of him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.”
2026-12-30.t: Sixth Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord

2026-12-31.a: The Holy Night by Correggio, about 1528–30, one of the first paintings in which all the light comes from the newborn Child. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
2026-12-31.b: “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth; we have beheld his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father.”
2026-12-31.m: Commemoration of Saint Sylvester I, Pope

o.a: The Legend of Saint Sylvester by Agnolo Gaddi, about 1380–85. Legend tells how the pope tamed a dragon that was poisoning Rome. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
o.b: Pope during the reign of Constantine, when the Church emerged from persecution. In his time the first great basilicas of Rome were built and the Council of Nicaea was held.

2026-12-31.t: Seventh Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord

2027-01-01.a: The Virgin of Vladimir, painted in Constantinople in the early 1100s and sent as a gift to Kiev. The Child presses his cheek to his mother's—the tender image called Eleousa, 'merciful'. It was credited with saving Moscow from Tamerlane, and is in the Tretyakov Gallery's church of St. Nicholas.
2027-01-01.b: On the octave day of Christmas the Church honors Mary under her greatest title, Theotokos, the Mother of God, and begins the new year in her care.
2027-01-01.t: The Octave Day of the Nativity of the Lord: Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God

2027-01-02.a: Saint Basil by Peter Paul Rubens, an oil sketch from the early 1600s, showing the bishop in his vestments, deep in thought. It is in the Ducal Museum at Friedenstein Castle, Gotha, Germany.
2027-01-02.b: Two friends from Cappadocia who studied together in Athens and became bishops and great defenders of the faith in the Trinity. Basil also wrote a rule for monks; Gregory was called 'the Theologian'.
2027-01-02.t: Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, Bishops and Doctors of the Church

2027-01-03.a: The Adoration of the Kings by Hugo van der Goes, about 1470, called the Monforte Altarpiece after the Spanish monastery of Monforte de Lemos, where it stayed until 1914. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-01-03.b: Wise men from the East follow a star to Bethlehem and kneel before the child with gold, frankincense and myrrh. Christ is revealed to all the nations.

2027-01-04.a: Elizabeth Ann Bayley Seton by Charles Balthazar Julien Févret de Saint-Mémin, 1797, when she was a young New York wife and mother. The French émigré made precise profile portraits using a tracing machine called a physiognotrace. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-01-04.b: A New York widow and convert who founded the Sisters of Charity and opened a free Catholic school at Emmitsburg, a seed of America's parish schools. The first native-born American saint.
2027-01-04.by: Charles Balthazar Julien Févret de Saint-Mémin

2027-01-05.a: Bishop John Neumann, engraved by Samuel Hollyer, 1892. The Bohemian immigrant became Bishop of Philadelphia and built the first diocesan Catholic school system in America. It is in the Library of Congress.
2027-01-05.b: A Bohemian immigrant who became bishop of Philadelphia. He built the first diocesan Catholic school system in the United States and was the first American bishop to be canonized.

2027-01-06.a: Brother André as an old man. For forty years the humble doorman of a Montreal school, he became famous for healings, and the crutches left by pilgrims still line the walls of St. Joseph's Oratory, the great basilica he inspired.
2027-01-06.b: A frail, barely literate Holy Cross brother who served for decades as doorkeeper of a Montreal college. His prayers to St. Joseph drew thousands of the sick, and he built the great Oratory of St. Joseph on Mount Royal.

o.a: Brother André as an old man. For forty years the humble doorman of a Montreal school, he became famous for healings, and the crutches left by pilgrims still line the walls of St. Joseph's Oratory, the great basilica he inspired.
o.b: A frail, barely literate Holy Cross brother who served for decades as doorkeeper of a Montreal college. His prayers to St. Joseph drew thousands of the sick, and he built the great Oratory of St. Joseph on Mount Royal.

w.a: The Disciples See Christ Walking on the Water by Henry Ossawa Tanner, about 1907. From their boat in the night the disciples make out a figure of light coming toward them across the sea. It is in the Des Moines Art Center.
w.b: “Take heart, it is I; have no fear.”
w.t: Wednesday after the Epiphany of the Lord

2027-01-07.a: The Virgin and Child with Saint Barbara and Saint Raymond of Penyafort, by Orazio Samacchini, painted on copper in 16th-century Bologna. Raymond is said to have sailed home from Majorca on his own cloak. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Chartres.
2027-01-07.b: A Dominican canon lawyer who compiled the Church's decrees and served as Master of his order. Legend says he sailed from Majorca on his cloak.

o.a: The Virgin and Child with Saint Barbara and Saint Raymond of Penyafort, by Orazio Samacchini, painted on copper in 16th-century Bologna. Raymond is said to have sailed home from Majorca on his own cloak. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Chartres.
o.b: A Dominican canon lawyer who compiled the Church's decrees and served as Master of his order. Legend says he sailed from Majorca on his cloak.

w.a: Jesus in the Synagogue by the Danish painter Joakim Skovgaard, 1914, a study for his altarpiece in Herning Church in Jutland. Jesus stands with the scroll of Isaiah before the people of Nazareth.
w.b: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
w.t: Thursday after the Epiphany of the Lord

2027-01-08.a: The Cleansing of the Leper from the Codex Egberti, about 980, one of the earliest picture cycles of the life of Christ, painted at Reichenau for Archbishop Egbert of Trier. It is in the City Library of Trier.
2027-01-08.b: “He stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, ‘I will; be clean.’ And immediately the leprosy left him.”
2027-01-08.t: Friday after the Epiphany of the Lord

2027-01-09.a: Saint John the Baptist by Leonardo da Vinci, about 1513–16, probably his last painting. John smiles out of the darkness and points upward to the one who must increase. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-01-09.b: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
2027-01-09.t: Saturday after the Epiphany of the Lord

2027-01-10.a: The Baptism of Christ by Andrea del Verrocchio and his pupil Leonardo da Vinci, about 1470–75. The young Leonardo painted the angel at far left; Vasari says Verrocchio was so outdone he gave up painting. It is in the Uffizi, Florence.
2027-01-10.b: Jesus is baptized by John in the Jordan. The heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice declares, 'This is my beloved Son.'
2027-01-10.by: Andrea del Verrocchio / Leonardo da Vinci

2027-01-11.a: The Calling of Peter and Andrew by Duccio, 1308–11, a panel from the back of his great Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-01-11.b: “Immediately they left their nets and followed him.”
2027-01-11.t: Monday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-12.a: Christ Preaching, called 'La Petite Tombe', an etching by Rembrandt, about 1652. Listeners of every age crowd around Christ, who teaches 'as one having authority'. This impression is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.
2027-01-12.b: “They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.”
2027-01-12.t: Tuesday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-13.a: Saint Martin and Saint Hilary, a Flemish embroidered roundel of about 1430–35, once sewn onto a priest's vestment. Hilary was the bishop who first welcomed the young soldier Martin to Poitiers. It is in the Robert Lehman Collection of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.
2027-01-13.b: A married pagan philosopher who became a Christian and Bishop of Poitiers. Exiled for defending the divinity of Christ, he wrote a great work on the Trinity and was teacher to St. Martin.

o.a: Saint Martin and Saint Hilary, a Flemish embroidered roundel of about 1430–35, once sewn onto a priest's vestment. Hilary was the bishop who first welcomed the young soldier Martin to Poitiers. It is in the Robert Lehman Collection of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.
o.b: A married pagan philosopher who became a Christian and Bishop of Poitiers. Exiled for defending the divinity of Christ, he wrote a great work on the Trinity and was teacher to St. Martin.
o.t: Saint Hilary, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-01-13.t: Saint Hilary, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

w.a: On the Sea of Galilee by Vasily Polenov, 1888, one of the paintings from his long journey through Palestine. Christ walks alone along the shore of the lake, deep in thought. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
w.b: “Let us go on to the next towns, that I may preach there also; for that is why I came out.”
w.t: Wednesday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-14.a: Christ and the Lepers by Gebhard Fugel, about 1920, a Bavarian painter of churches and Bible scenes. The lepers kneel at the roadside as Christ stops for them.
2027-01-14.b: “If you will, you can make me clean.”
2027-01-14.t: Thursday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-15.a: Christ Healing the Paralytic by Anthony van Dyck and his workshop, about 1621. 'Rise, take up your mat, and walk.'
2027-01-15.b: “I say to you, rise, take up your pallet and go home.”
2027-01-15.t: Friday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-16.a: The Feast in the House of Levi by Paolo Veronese, 1573, over 42 feet wide. Painted as a Last Supper, it was so crowded with dogs, jesters and soldiers that the Inquisition summoned Veronese; he simply renamed it after Levi's banquet. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
2027-01-16.b: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.”
2027-01-16.t: Saturday of the first week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-17.a: Ecce Agnus Dei by Dieric Bouts, about 1462–64. John the Baptist points out Jesus walking past to a kneeling donor: 'Behold the Lamb of God.' It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.
2027-01-17.b: “He said to them, ‘Come and see.’ They came and saw where he was staying; and they stayed with him that day.”

2027-01-18.a: The Wedding at Cana by Paolo Veronese, 1562–63, the largest painting in the Louvre. Napoleon's troops took it from the refectory of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice; it now faces the Mona Lisa.
2027-01-18.b: “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.”
2027-01-18.t: Monday of the second week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-19.a: August, by Marten van Valckenborch, about 1585, from a series of the months, each with a Gospel scene. In the harvest fields, Christ defends his disciples for picking grain on the sabbath.
2027-01-19.b: “So the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.”
2027-01-19.t: Tuesday of the second week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-20.a: Saint Sebastian by Andrea Mantegna, about 1457–59. Pierced with arrows, he stands against a ruined Roman arch; Mantegna signed his name in Greek on the pillar, and a horseman hides in the clouds. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-01-20.b: A Roman soldier who encouraged Christians in prison. Shot with arrows and left for dead, he survived, confronted the emperor, and was martyred.

o.a: The Madonna Enthroned with Saints by Paris Bordone, about 1530, a Venetian pupil of Titian. Pope Fabian, martyred in 250, joins the saints around the throne. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
o.b: Chosen pope, the story goes, when a dove settled on his head. He organized the Church of Rome and died a martyr under the emperor Decius.

o.a: Saint Sebastian by Andrea Mantegna, about 1457–59. Pierced with arrows, he stands against a ruined Roman arch; Mantegna signed his name in Greek on the pillar, and a horseman hides in the clouds. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
o.b: A Roman soldier who encouraged Christians in prison. Shot with arrows and left for dead, he survived, confronted the emperor, and was martyred.

w.a: The Healing of the Man with the Withered Hand, a fresco in the Chapel of the Holy Trinity at Lublin Castle, Poland, finished in 1418. Painters from Ruthenia covered the Gothic chapel in Byzantine-style frescoes for King Władysław II Jagiełło.
w.b: “Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life or to kill?”
w.by: Ruthenian painters under Master Andrew (photo: Hans A. Rosbach)
w.t: Wednesday of the second week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-21.a: Saint Agnes in Prison by Jusepe de Ribera, 1641. Stripped and exposed, she prays as her hair grows to cover her and an angel brings a white cloth from heaven. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
2027-01-21.b: A girl of about twelve who refused marriage, saying she was already promised to Christ, and was put to death in Rome. Her name is said in the Roman Canon of the Mass, and she is often shown with a lamb.

2027-01-22.a: The Madonna del Parto (Madonna of Childbirth) by Piero della Francesca, about 1460, one of the very few paintings of Mary expecting. Two angels draw back a tent as she rests her hand on her unborn child. It is in its own small museum in Monterchi, Tuscany.
2027-01-22.b: A day of prayer and penance in the United States for the protection of human life, entrusted to Our Lady of Guadalupe, patroness of the unborn.

o.a: The Madonna del Parto (Madonna of Childbirth) by Piero della Francesca, about 1460, one of the very few paintings of Mary expecting. Two angels draw back a tent as she rests her hand on her unborn child. It is in its own small museum in Monterchi, Tuscany.
o.b: A day of prayer and penance in the United States for the protection of human life, entrusted to Our Lady of Guadalupe, patroness of the unborn.
o.t: Day of Prayer for the Legal Protection of Unborn Children

2027-01-22.t: Day of Prayer for the Legal Protection of Unborn Children

w.a: The Synaxis of the Twelve Apostles, an icon painted in Constantinople in the early 1300s. The twelve stand together in two rows, with Peter and Paul at the front. It is in the Pushkin Museum, Moscow.
w.b: “And he appointed twelve, to be with him, and to be sent out to preach.”
w.t: Friday of the second week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-23.a: Saints Vincent, James and Eustace by Antonio and Piero del Pollaiuolo, 1467–68, made for the Chapel of the Cardinal of Portugal at San Miniato al Monte, Florence. It is in the Uffizi; a copy stands in the chapel.
2027-01-23.b: A deacon of Saragossa in Spain, tortured to death at Valencia under Diocletian. He is the first martyr of Spain and patron of winemakers.
2027-01-23.by: Antonio del Pollaiuolo / Piero del Pollaiuolo

o.a: Saints Vincent, James and Eustace by Antonio and Piero del Pollaiuolo, 1467–68, made for the Chapel of the Cardinal of Portugal at San Miniato al Monte, Florence. It is in the Uffizi; a copy stands in the chapel.
o.b: A deacon of Saragossa in Spain, tortured to death at Valencia under Diocletian. He is the first martyr of Spain and patron of winemakers.
o.by: Antonio del Pollaiuolo / Piero del Pollaiuolo

o.a: Mother Marianne Cope, who in 1883 led six Franciscan sisters from Syracuse, New York, to care for leprosy patients in Hawaii. She nursed Father Damien in his last days and never caught the disease.
o.b: A Franciscan sister from Syracuse, New York, who led nuns to care for leprosy patients in Hawaiʻi and continued Father Damien's work on Molokaʻi.

w.a: Christ Preaching to the Multitudes by the English painter James Smetham (1821–1889), a friend of Rossetti and Ruskin. The crowd presses so close around Jesus that there is hardly room to move.
w.b: “And when his friends heard it, they went out to seize him, for they said, ‘He is beside himself.’”
w.t: Saturday of the second week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-24.a: The Calling of the First Apostles by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1481, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. Peter and Andrew kneel before Christ on the shore of Galilee, while in the distance Jesus calls James and John from their boat.
2027-01-24.b: “Follow me and I will make you become fishers of men.”
2027-01-24.t: Third Sunday in Ordinary Time, or Sunday of the Word of God

2027-01-25.a: The Conversion on the Way to Damascus by Caravaggio, 1601. Saul lies on his back beneath his horse, arms flung open to a light only he can see. It still hangs where it was made for, in the Cerasi Chapel of Santa Maria del Popolo, Rome.
2027-01-25.b: On the road to Damascus to arrest Christians, Saul is thrown to the ground by a light from heaven and hears, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?' The persecutor becomes the Apostle to the Gentiles.
2027-01-25.t: The Conversion of Saint Paul the Apostle

2027-01-26.a: The Saints of the 22nd of January by Konstantinos Tzanes, a Cretan painter working in 17th-century Venice. It belongs to the Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies, Venice.
2027-01-26.b: Companions of St. Paul, who wrote them the 'pastoral letters'. Timothy led the church at Ephesus, Titus the church on Crete.

2027-01-27.a: A fresco in the chapel of Saint Angela Merici at Tiarno di Sotto, in the mountains of Trentino. Angela is shown with her first companions, the young women of Brescia who became the Ursulines.
2027-01-27.b: An Italian laywoman who saw that girls needed education in the faith. In Brescia she founded the Ursulines, the first order of women devoted to teaching.

o.a: A fresco in the chapel of Saint Angela Merici at Tiarno di Sotto, in the mountains of Trentino. Angela is shown with her first companions, the young women of Brescia who became the Ursulines.
o.b: An Italian laywoman who saw that girls needed education in the faith. In Brescia she founded the Ursulines, the first order of women devoted to teaching.

w.a: Landscape with the Parable of the Sower by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1557. A sower scatters seed in the foreground while birds wait behind him and the river valley opens beyond. It is in the Timken Museum of Art, San Diego.
w.b: “And other seeds fell into good soil and brought forth grain, growing up and increasing and yielding thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold.”
w.t: Wednesday of the third week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-28.a: The Apotheosis of Saint Thomas Aquinas by Francisco de Zurbarán, 1631, one of his largest paintings, made for the Dominican college of St. Thomas in Seville. Thomas rises among the Doctors of the Church as the emperor Charles V kneels below. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Seville.
2027-01-28.b: A Dominican friar and the Church's great theologian. His Summa Theologiae united faith and reason; he is the 'Angelic Doctor' and patron of students.
2027-01-28.t: Saint Thomas Aquinas, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-01-29.a: Wheatfield with a Reaper by Vincent van Gogh, 1889, painted from his window at Saint-Rémy. 'When the grain is ripe, he wields the sickle at once.' Van Gogh wrote that he saw in the reaper an image of death, 'in the great book of nature'. It is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
2027-01-29.b: “The kingdom of God is as if a man should scatter seed upon the ground, and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should sprout and grow, he knows not how.”
2027-01-29.t: Friday of the third week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-30.a: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee by Rembrandt, 1633, his only seascape. It was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston in 1990 and has never been found; its empty frame still hangs there.
2027-01-30.b: “He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, ‘Peace! Be still!’ And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.”
2027-01-30.t: Saturday of the third week of Ordinary Time

2027-01-31.a: Jesus Healing a Man Possessed by a Devil, by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Doré's 241 Bible engravings were reprinted around the world and shaped how generations pictured the Gospels.
2027-01-31.b: “What is this? A new teaching! With authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.”

2027-02-01.a: Christ Heals the Possessed Man in the Region of the Gerasenes, a 17th-century Dutch print; the swine rush down the slope into the sea. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-02-01.b: “Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you.”
2027-02-01.t: Monday of the fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-02-02.a: The Presentation in the Temple by Andrea Mantegna, about 1454. The figures at the edges may be Mantegna himself and his wife Nicolosia, sister of Giovanni Bellini. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-02-02.b: Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple, where old Simeon takes him in his arms and calls him 'a light for revelation to the Gentiles.' Candles are blessed today.

2027-02-03.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Blaise by Gaspar de Crayer, 1668, painted when the Flemish artist was in his eighties. The bishop is tortured with iron combs before his beheading. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Ghent.
2027-02-03.b: A bishop of Armenia who, tradition says, saved a boy choking on a fishbone. The blessing of throats is given on his feast.

o.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Blaise by Gaspar de Crayer, 1668, painted when the Flemish artist was in his eighties. The bishop is tortured with iron combs before his beheading. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Ghent.
o.b: A bishop of Armenia who, tradition says, saved a boy choking on a fishbone. The blessing of throats is given on his feast.

o.a: Ansgar Preaching Christianity by Gustaf Cederström, 1889, a design for a mural in Sweden's Nationalmuseum. The monk preaches to the pagan Swedes at Birka, the first Christian mission in the country. It is in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
o.b: A Benedictine monk who carried the Gospel to Denmark and Sweden and became the first Archbishop of Hamburg. He is called the Apostle of the North.

w.a: Christ in the House of His Parents ('The Carpenter's Shop') by John Everett Millais, 1849–50. In Joseph's workshop the boy Jesus has cut his palm on a nail, and Mary kneels to comfort him. It is in Tate Britain, London.
w.b: “And he marveled because of their unbelief. And he went about among the villages teaching.”
w.t: Wednesday of the fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-02-04.a: The Mission of the Apostles, the great tympanum over the central door of the Basilica of Vézelay in Burgundy, carved about 1130. Rays from Christ's hands fall on the apostles, sent to every people of the earth.
2027-02-04.b: “He called to him the twelve, and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.”
2027-02-04.t: Thursday of the fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-02-05.a: Saint Agatha by Francisco de Zurbarán, about 1630–33, painted for a Mercedarian monastery in Seville. Dressed in rich silks, she calmly carries the emblem of her martyrdom on a plate. It is in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
2027-02-05.b: A young Christian of Sicily who refused the advances of a Roman official and was tortured and imprisoned for her faith. She died in prison at Catania and is invoked against fire and breast disease.

2027-02-06.a: The Martyrs of Nagasaki, a painting from Prague. The twenty-six martyrs of 1597 are raised on crosses on a hill above Nagasaki and pierced with lances.
2027-02-06.b: A Japanese Jesuit, son of a samurai, who was crucified at Nagasaki with twenty-five companions—priests, brothers, laymen and boys. From the cross he forgave his executioners.
2027-02-06.t: Saint Paul Miki and Companions, Martyrs

2027-02-07.a: Jesus and Peter's Mother-in-Law, from the Hitda Codex, a Gospel book made in Cologne around 1020 for Abbess Hitda of Meschede. Christ takes the sick woman by the hand. It is in the University and State Library, Darmstadt.
2027-02-07.b: “In the morning, a great while before day, he rose and went out to a lonely place, and there he prayed.”

2027-02-08.a: Josephine Bakhita in her religious habit. Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was so traumatized she forgot her own name; 'Bakhita', meaning 'fortunate', was given by her captors.
2027-02-08.b: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was freed in Italy, became a Canossian sister and was loved for her gentleness. She is patron of Sudan and of victims of trafficking.

o.a: Saint Jerome Emiliani by Giandomenico Tiepolo, 1759, from the private chapel of the Tiepolo family villa at Zianigo. It is now in Ca' Rezzonico, Venice.
o.b: A Venetian soldier who was captured in war and freed, he believed, by Mary's help. He gave his life to orphans and the homeless and is patron of orphans and abandoned children.

o.a: Josephine Bakhita in her religious habit. Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was so traumatized she forgot her own name; 'Bakhita', meaning 'fortunate', was given by her captors.
o.b: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was freed in Italy, became a Canossian sister and was loved for her gentleness. She is patron of Sudan and of victims of trafficking.

w.a: Jesus Teaching on the Seashore by James Tissot, one of some 350 watercolors of the life of Christ he painted between 1886 and 1894 after travels in the Holy Land. The people of the lakeside towns crowd down to the water to see him. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
w.b: “And wherever he came, in villages, cities, or country, they laid the sick in the market places, and besought him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched it were made well.”
w.t: Monday of the fifth week of Ordinary Time

2027-02-09.a: Christ among the Pharisees by Jacob Jordaens, 17th century. The Pharisees press around Christ with their books of the Law, arguing over the traditions of the elders.
2027-02-09.b: “You leave the commandment of God, and hold fast the tradition of men.”
2027-02-09.t: Tuesday of the fifth week of Ordinary Time

2027-02-10.a: Christ in the Wilderness by Ivan Kramskoi, 1872. Christ sits alone among stones at dawn, his hands clenched, after forty days of fasting. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
2027-02-10.b: The first day of Lent. Ashes are marked on the forehead with the words, 'Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return.'

2027-02-11.a: Christ Carrying the Cross by Titian, about 1565. Simon of Cyrene leans in to share the weight as Christ turns his face toward us. It is in the Prado, Madrid.
2027-02-11.b: “If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.”
2027-02-11.m: Commemoration of Our Lady of Lourdes

o.a: Our Lady of Lourdes by Virgilio Tojetti, 1877. Bernadette kneels before the Lady in the grotto of Massabielle, where eighteen apparitions took place in 1858.
o.b: In 1858 the Virgin Mary appeared eighteen times to Bernadette Soubirous at Lourdes, calling herself 'the Immaculate Conception'. The spring there has drawn countless pilgrims and sick people.

2027-02-12.a: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1559. In a crowded Flemish square, fat Carnival astride a barrel jousts with gaunt Lent, whose lance is a baker's paddle holding two herrings; half the town feasts, the other half fasts, prays and gives alms. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-02-12.b: “Can the wedding guests mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? The days will come, when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.”

2027-02-13.a: The Calling of Saint Matthew, after Jan Sanders van Hemessen, 16th century. Levi, among his ledgers and coins, looks up as Christ calls him. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-02-13.b: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

2027-02-14.a: The Temptations of Christ by Sandro Botticelli, 1481–82, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. The devil, disguised as a hermit, tempts Christ three times in the background, while in front a priest performs a sacrifice at the Temple.
2027-02-14.b: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent, and believe in the gospel.”

2027-02-15.a: The Last Judgment by Stefan Lochner, about 1435, the great painter of Cologne. Christ judges from a rainbow; on the left the saved are led by angels into a Gothic heaven, on the right devils drag the damned to hell. It is in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.
2027-02-15.b: “Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you did it to me.”
2027-02-15.t: Monday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-16.a: Christ Teaching the Apostles the Lord's Prayer, a 16th-century German engraving by Hans Brosamer. It is in the collection of the Leiden University Library.
2027-02-16.b: “Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
2027-02-16.t: Tuesday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-17.a: The prophet Jonah by Michelangelo, painted about 1511 on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, directly above the altar. He leans back to look up at God, the great fish behind him; his three days in its belly became the 'sign of Jonah', a sign of the Resurrection.
2027-02-17.b: “This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, but no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah.”
2027-02-17.m: Commemoration of the Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order

o.a: The Madonna Presents the Dead Christ to the Seven Holy Founders, by Gaspare Diziani, about 1750. The seven Florentine merchants left their businesses in 1233 to found the Servants of Mary.
o.b: Seven merchants of Florence who left their businesses to live together in prayer and penance, founding the Order of Servants of Mary.
o.t: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order

2027-02-17.t: Wednesday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-18.a: The Light of the World by William Holman Hunt. Christ knocks at an overgrown door that has no handle on the outside. This large final version, finished in 1904, toured the world and now hangs in St. Paul's Cathedral, London.
2027-02-18.b: “Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.”
2027-02-18.t: Thursday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-19.a: Cain Slaying Abel by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1608–09. Cain stands over his brother, about to strike, beside the smoking altar of their offerings: 'whoever is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment.' It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
2027-02-19.b: “So if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.”
2027-02-19.t: Friday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-20.a: Landscape with the Good Samaritan by Rembrandt, 1638 — love for one's enemy. The tiny figure of the Samaritan leads the wounded man to the inn under a stormy sky. It is in the Czartoryski Museum, Kraków.
2027-02-20.b: “So that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust.”
2027-02-20.t: Saturday of the first week of Lent

2027-02-21.a: The Transfiguration by Fra Angelico, about 1440, painted on the wall of a friar's cell in the convent of San Marco, Florence. Christ stands with arms outstretched in a blaze of white light, foreshadowing the cross.
2027-02-21.b: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

2027-02-22.a: The Cathedra Petri by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1657–66, at the far end of St. Peter's Basilica. A gilded bronze throne held aloft by four Doctors of the Church encloses an ancient wooden chair, beneath a window of the Holy Spirit.
2027-02-22.b: A feast of the authority Christ gave Peter to teach and lead his Church: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.' The chair is a symbol of the pope's office.
2027-02-22.t: The Chair of Saint Peter the Apostle

2027-02-23.a: Christ Washing the Feet of the Disciples by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1575–80. Christ kneels to wash Peter's feet while the others look on: the greatest among them as their servant. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-02-23.b: “He who is greatest among you shall be your servant; whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
2027-02-23.m: Commemoration of Saint Polycarp, Bishop and Martyr

o.a: The Procession of the Holy Martyrs in Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna, about 560. Polycarp walks among a line of white-robed martyrs carrying their crowns toward Christ.
o.b: Bishop of Smyrna and a disciple of St. John the Apostle. Told to curse Christ, he answered, 'Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong,' and was burned alive.
o.by: Meister von San Apollinare Nuovo in Ravenna

2027-02-23.t: Tuesday of the second week of Lent

2027-02-24.a: The Agony in the Garden by Giovanni Bellini, about 1458–60. Christ prays on a rock as dawn breaks and the disciples sleep; Judas and the soldiers are already on their way. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-02-24.b: “Even as the Son of man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
2027-02-24.t: Wednesday of the second week of Lent

2027-02-25.a: The Rich Man and Lazarus by Luca Giordano, 17th century. The poor man lies at the gate while the rich man feasts. It is in the Harvard Art Museums, Cambridge, Massachusetts.
2027-02-25.b: “Son, remember that you in your lifetime received your good things, and Lazarus in like manner evil things; but now he is comforted here, and you are in anguish.”
2027-02-25.t: Thursday of the second week of Lent

2027-02-26.a: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants by Domenico Fetti, about 1618–22, from his series of small paintings of the parables. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Dresden.
2027-02-26.b: “Afterward he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’”
2027-02-26.t: Friday of the second week of Lent

2027-02-27.a: The Return of the Prodigal Son by Rembrandt, about 1668, painted near the end of his life. The ragged son kneels with his head against his father's chest, and the father's two hands rest on his back. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.
2027-02-27.b: “While he was yet at a distance, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him.”
2027-02-27.m: Commemoration of Saint Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor of the Church

o.a: The oldest portrait of Gregory of Narek, from a manuscript of his Book of Lamentations copied in 1173, less than two centuries after his death. It is in the Matenadaran, the great library of ancient manuscripts in Yerevan, Armenia.
o.b: An Armenian monk and poet whose Book of Lamentations is a classic of Armenian literature. Named a Doctor of the Church in 2015.
o.t: Saint Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor of the Church

2027-02-27.t: Saturday of the second week of Lent

2027-02-28.a: Christ Driving the Traders from the Temple by El Greco, about 1600. He painted the subject again and again over his career; Christ swings the whip in the middle of a tangle of falling bodies and overturned tables.
2027-02-28.b: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

2027-03-01.a: The People of Nazareth Drive Christ out of the Town, a 17th-century engraving made for the Gospel of this very day, the Monday of the third week of Lent. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-03-01.b: “But passing through the midst of them he went away.”
2027-03-01.t: Monday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-02.a: The Parable of the Unmerciful Servant by Jan Sanders van Hemessen, about 1556. The king's steward reads out the huge debt while the servant begs for time. It is in the University of Michigan Museum of Art, Ann Arbor.
2027-03-02.b: “Should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?”
2027-03-02.t: Tuesday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-03.a: Christ among the Doctors by Albrecht Dürer, 1506, painted in Venice in five days, as the note tucked into the book at the left says. Old teachers of the Law crowd around the boy Jesus with their books. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
2027-03-03.b: “Think not that I have come to abolish the law and the prophets; I have come not to abolish them but to fulfil them.”
2027-03-03.m: Commemoration of Saint Katharine Drexel, Virgin

o.a: Mother Katharine Drexel around 1915. Heiress to a Philadelphia banking fortune, she gave about twenty million dollars to found schools for Native American and Black students, including Xavier University in New Orleans.
o.b: A Philadelphia heiress who gave her fortune and life to found schools for Native American and Black students, including Xavier University of Louisiana.

2027-03-03.t: Wednesday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-04.a: Jesus Heals a Mute Possessed Man by James Tissot, 1886–94, one of the hundreds of watercolors of his Life of Christ, made after his journeys to the Holy Land. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
2027-03-04.b: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters.”

o.a: The 'three-handed' Saint Casimir in his chapel in Vilnius Cathedral, Lithuania, painted around 1600. Legend says the painter tried to paint over a misplaced hand, but it kept reappearing, so he left all three.
o.b: A Polish prince known for his prayer, purity and generosity to the poor. He died young of tuberculosis and is patron of Poland and Lithuania.

2027-03-04.t: Thursday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-05.a: The Good Samaritan (after Delacroix) by Vincent van Gogh, 1890, painted at Saint-Rémy from a print of Delacroix's picture — 'love your neighbor as yourself.' It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.
2027-03-05.b: “When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, ‘You are not far from the kingdom of God.’ And after that no one dared to ask him any question.”
2027-03-05.by: After Eugène Delacroix / Vincent van Gogh
2027-03-05.t: Friday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-06.a: Church Interior with the Pharisee and the Publican by Dirck van Delen, 17th century. In a vast imaginary church, the Pharisee stands boldly in front while the tax collector hangs back at the edge. It is in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts.
2027-03-06.b: “I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for every one who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
2027-03-06.t: Saturday of the third week of Lent

2027-03-07.a: Nicodemus Visiting Jesus by Henry Ossawa Tanner, 1899, painted after his first journey to the Holy Land. They talk by night on a rooftop in Jerusalem. Tanner was the first African American painter to win international fame. It is in the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts.
2027-03-07.b: “For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”

2027-03-08.a: Jesus Heals the Nobleman's Son, a Mughal painting from a Mirror of Holiness, the life of Christ the Jesuit Jerome Xavier wrote in Persian for the emperor Akbar, illustrated at Allahabad, India, about 1602–04. It is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.
2027-03-08.b: “Jesus said to him, ‘Go; your son will live.’ The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and went his way.”
2027-03-08.m: Commemoration of Saint John of God, Religious

o.a: Saint John of God Carrying a Sick Man by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1672. Exhausted, he stumbles under his burden, and an angel steps in to help him. It hangs in the Hospital de la Caridad, Seville.
o.b: A Portuguese shepherd, soldier and bookseller who, after a dramatic conversion, opened a hospital in Granada for the poor and sick. His followers became the Brothers Hospitallers.

2027-03-08.t: Monday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-09.a: Christ Healing the Paralytic at the Pool of Bethesda by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1667–70, painted for the Hospital de la Caridad in Seville. The man who has waited thirty-eight years looks up as Christ tells him to rise. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-03-09.b: “Jesus said to him, ‘Rise, take up your pallet, and walk.’ And at once the man was healed, and he took up his pallet and walked.”
2027-03-09.m: Commemoration of Saint Frances of Rome, Religious

o.a: Head of Saint Francesca Romana by Orazio Gentileschi, about 1618. Gentileschi was the father of the painter Artemisia. It is on deposit at the Petit Palais, Paris.
o.b: A Roman noblewoman, wife and mother, who spent her wealth on the poor during plague and famine. She founded a community of women to serve them, and it was said her guardian angel was visible to her.

2027-03-09.t: Tuesday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-10.a: The Holy Trinity by Masaccio, about 1427, one of the first paintings to use true perspective. The Father holds up the cross of the Son, and the dove of the Spirit passes between them. It is in Santa Maria Novella, Florence.
2027-03-10.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me, has eternal life; he does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.”
2027-03-10.t: Wednesday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-11.a: Moses with the Ten Commandments by Rembrandt, 1659. Moses raises the tablets of the Law above his head — 'he wrote about me.' It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-03-11.b: “You search the scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness to me; yet you refuse to come to me that you may have life.”
2027-03-11.t: Thursday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-12.a: Christ Preaching to the Elders in the Temple by John Martin, 19th century. It is in the Yale Center for British Art, New Haven.
2027-03-12.b: “You know me, and you know where I come from? But I have not come of my own accord; he who sent me is true, and him you do not know. I know him, for I come from him, and he sent me.”
2027-03-12.t: Friday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-13.a: Christ Instructing Nicodemus by Jacob Jordaens, about 1650. It is in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts, Brussels.
2027-03-13.b: “No man ever spoke like this man!”
2027-03-13.t: Saturday of the fourth week of Lent

2027-03-14.a: The Crucifixion from the Isenheim Altarpiece by Matthias Grünewald, 1512–16, painted for a monastery hospital that cared for victims of a terrible skin disease. Christ's body bears their sores. It is in the Unterlinden Museum, Colmar, France.
2027-03-14.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”

2027-03-15.a: The Woman Taken in Adultery by Rembrandt, 1644. In the vast golden Temple, the woman kneels in white before Christ while her accusers press around. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-03-15.b: “She said, ‘No one, Lord.’ And Jesus said, ‘Neither do I condemn you; go, and do not sin again.’”
2027-03-15.t: Monday of the fifth week of Lent

2027-03-16.a: The Crucifixion by Andrea Mantegna, 1457–59, from the predella of the San Zeno altarpiece in Verona. 'When you lift up the Son of Man.' It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-03-16.b: “He who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.”
2027-03-16.t: Tuesday of the fifth week of Lent

2027-03-17.a: 'What Is Truth?' Christ and Pilate, by Nikolai Ge, 1890. Pilate, in full sunlight, turns away with his question; Christ stands silent in the shadow. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
2027-03-17.b: “If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”

o.a: Saint Patrick, Bishop of Ireland, by Giambattista Tiepolo, 1746, painted for a church in Padua. Patrick raises his hand in blessing over a sick man at his feet. It is in the Musei Civici, Padua.
o.b: Kidnapped from Britain as a boy and enslaved in Ireland, he escaped, became a priest, and returned to convert the Irish. Legend says he used the shamrock to explain the Trinity.

2027-03-17.t: Wednesday of the fifth week of Lent

2027-03-18.a: The Jews Took Up Rocks to Stone Jesus by James Tissot, 1886–96, from his Life of Christ. The crowd snatches up stones from the Temple works as Christ slips away. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
2027-03-18.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am.”
2027-03-18.m: Commemoration of Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

o.a: A painting by Palma il Giovane, about 1590, in the sacristy of the Chiesa dei Gesuiti in Venice. Cyril of Jerusalem appears in a cycle on the legendary history of the Crutched Friars.
o.b: Bishop of Jerusalem, exiled three times in the controversies of his age. His lectures to those preparing for baptism give a vivid picture of the early Church's faith and worship.
o.t: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-03-18.t: Thursday of the fifth week of Lent

2027-03-19.a: The Marriage of the Virgin by Raphael, 1504, painted at twenty-one and proudly signed on the temple. Joseph holds the rod that miraculously blossomed to show he was God's choice; a rejected suitor breaks his over his knee. It is in the Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan.
2027-03-19.b: A carpenter of Nazareth, a just and silent man, who took Mary as his wife and raised Jesus as his own son. He is patron of the universal Church, of fathers and of a happy death.
2027-03-19.t: Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-03-20.a: Christ before the High Priest by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1617. Lit by a single candle, the high priest raises his finger as Christ stands calmly before him. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-03-20.b: “You do not understand that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.”
2027-03-20.t: Saturday of the fifth week of Lent

2027-03-21.a: The Entry into Jerusalem by Jan Baegert, about 1505–10, from the wing of an altarpiece. It is in the City Museum of Münster, Germany.
2027-03-21.b: Jesus enters Jerusalem to the cries of 'Hosanna!', the crowds laying palms before him. Holy Week begins.
2027-03-21.t: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord

2027-03-22.a: Mary Anointing the Feet of Christ by the Master of Perea, a late 15th-century Spanish painter from Valencia. It is in the Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven.
2027-03-22.b: “Mary took a pound of costly ointment of pure nard and anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.”

2027-03-23.a: The Last Supper by Philippe de Champaigne, 1652, painted for the convent of Port-Royal in Paris. The apostles look to one another as Jesus says, 'One of you will betray me.' It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-03-23.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, one of you will betray me.”

2027-03-24.a: Judas Returning the Thirty Pieces of Silver by Rembrandt, 1629, painted when he was twenty-three. Too late, Judas throws the coins down before the priests and elders, wringing his hands in despair.
2027-03-24.b: “Judas, who betrayed him, said, ‘Is it I, Master?’ He said to him, ‘You have said so.’”

2027-03-25.a: The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci, 1495–98, on the refectory wall of Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan. Leonardo shows the moment Jesus says 'One of you will betray me.' His experimental technique began flaking within his lifetime.
2027-03-25.b: Holy Thursday: at the Last Supper Jesus washes his disciples' feet, gives them his body and blood, and says, 'Do this in memory of me.'

2027-03-26.a: Christ Crucified by Diego Velázquez, about 1632, painted for the convent of San Plácido in Madrid. Alone against a dark background, it inspired a book-length poem by Miguel de Unamuno. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-03-26.b: Good Friday. Christ dies on the cross. 'Behold the wood of the Cross, on which hung the salvation of the world.'
2027-03-26.t: Friday of the Passion of the Lord

2027-03-27.a: The Entombment of Christ by Caravaggio, 1603–04, painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome. Nicodemus and John lower the body as the women grieve. Napoleon took it to Paris; it came back after his fall and is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.
2027-03-27.b: The Lord lies in the tomb. The Church waits in silence until the Easter Vigil, when the new fire is kindled in the dark.

2027-03-28.a: The Resurrection by Piero della Francesca, about 1463–65, in the town hall of Sansepolcro, Tuscany. Christ rises from the tomb above sleeping soldiers. The novelist Aldous Huxley called it 'the best picture in the world', and a British officer spared the town from shelling in 1944 because he remembered it.
2027-03-28.b: Christ is risen. The empty tomb at dawn is the heart of the Christian faith, and the Easter feast is kept for eight days as a single day of joy.
2027-03-28.t: Easter Sunday of the Resurrection of the Lord

2027-03-29.a: The Three Marys at the Tomb, about 1425–35, by Jan van Eyck and perhaps his brother Hubert. An angel sits on the open tomb while the soldiers sleep, with an imagined Jerusalem behind. It is in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam.
2027-03-29.b: “Behold, Jesus met them and said, ‘Hail!’ And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them, ‘Do not be afraid; go and tell my brethren to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.’”
2027-03-29.by: Attributed to Jan van Eyck / Attributed to Hubert van Eyck
2027-03-29.t: Monday within the Octave of Easter

2027-03-30.a: Noli me tangere by Fra Angelico, about 1440–42, painted on the wall of a friar's cell at the Convent of San Marco in Florence. Christ carries a hoe, as the gardener Mary takes him for, in a meadow scattered with flowers.
2027-03-30.b: “Jesus said to her, ‘Mary.’ She turned and said to him in Hebrew, ‘Rabboni!’ (which means Teacher).”
2027-03-30.t: Tuesday within the Octave of Easter

2027-03-31.a: The Supper at Emmaus by Caravaggio, 1601. The moment Christ blesses the bread, one disciple grips his chair and the other flings out his arms. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-03-31.b: “When he was at table with them, he took the bread and blessed, and broke it, and gave it to them. And their eyes were opened and they recognized him; and he vanished out of their sight.”
2027-03-31.t: Wednesday within the Octave of Easter

2027-04-01.a: Christ Appears Behind Locked Doors by Duccio, 1308–11, a panel from his great Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.
2027-04-01.t: Thursday within the Octave of Easter

2027-04-02.a: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes by Konrad Witz, 1444, from an altarpiece for Geneva Cathedral. It is often called the first realistic landscape in European art: the lake and mountains are the real view across Lake Geneva. It is in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Geneva.
2027-04-02.b: “That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, ‘It is the Lord!’ When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his clothes, for he was stripped for work, and sprang into the sea.”
2027-04-02.t: Friday within the Octave of Easter

2027-04-03.a: Christ and St Mary Magdalen at the Tomb by Rembrandt, 1638. Christ wears a gardener's hat and holds a spade, and dawn breaks over Jerusalem. It is in the Royal Collection, Buckingham Palace, London.
2027-04-03.b: “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to the whole creation.”
2027-04-03.t: Saturday within the Octave of Easter

2027-04-04.a: The original Divine Mercy image by Eugeniusz Kazimirowski, 1934, painted in Vilnius under St. Faustina's own direction. It hangs in the Divine Mercy Sanctuary in Vilnius, Lithuania.
2027-04-04.b: The Sunday after Easter, devoted to the mercy of Christ as revealed to St. Faustina Kowalska: 'Jesus, I trust in you.'
2027-04-04.t: Second Sunday of Easter or Sunday of Divine Mercy

2027-04-05.a: The Annunciation by Leonardo da Vinci, about 1472–76, painted when he was in his early twenties in Verrocchio's workshop in Florence. Gabriel kneels in a walled garden as Mary looks up from her book. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
2027-04-05.b: The angel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will bear the Son of God, and she answers, 'Let it be done to me according to your word.' Nine months before Christmas, the Word becomes flesh.

2027-04-06.a: The Brazen Serpent by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1635–40. Moses lifts up the bronze serpent and the dying Israelites who look at it are healed — Christ's own image for his cross. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-04-06.b: “As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.”
2027-04-06.t: Tuesday of the second week of Easter

2027-04-07.a: Jean-Baptiste de La Salle, engraved by L. Chapon after Charles Müller for an 1887 Life of the saint. He is shown as a teacher among his pupils, the poor boys of Reims for whom he founded his schools.
2027-04-07.b: A French priest who founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools and pioneered teacher training. He is patron of teachers.
2027-04-07.t: Saint John Baptist de la Salle, Priest

2027-04-08.a: Christ Pantocrator from St. Catherine's Monastery, Sinai, painted in wax in the 500s, one of the oldest icons in the world. The two sides of the face differ, showing Christ as both judge and merciful savior.
2027-04-08.b: “The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.”
2027-04-08.t: Thursday of the second week of Easter

2027-04-09.a: The Multiplication of the Loaves and Fishes by Paolo Farinati, in the church of San Giorgio in Braida, Verona. Five loaves and two fish feed five thousand.
2027-04-09.b: “Jesus then took the loaves, and when he had given thanks, he distributed them to those who were seated; so also the fish, as much as they wanted.”
2027-04-09.t: Friday of the second week of Easter

2027-04-10.a: Walking on the Water by Ivan Aivazovsky, 1888, the great Russian painter of the sea. Christ walks toward the boat across a moonlit, storm-churned sea. It is in the Museum of the History of Religion, St. Petersburg.
2027-04-10.b: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
2027-04-10.t: Saturday of the second week of Easter

2027-04-11.a: The Appearance While the Apostles Are at Table by Duccio, 1308–11, a small panel from his Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral. The risen Christ appears among the startled disciples at their meal. It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.
2027-04-11.b: “See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; handle me, and see; for a spirit has not flesh and bones as you see that I have.”

2027-04-12.a: Christ Preaching at Capernaum by Maurycy Gottlieb, 1878–79, left unfinished when the young Polish-Jewish painter died at 23. Christ, in a prayer shawl, teaches in the synagogue. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.
2027-04-12.b: “Do not labor for the food which perishes, but for the food which endures to eternal life, which the Son of man will give to you; for on him has God the Father set his seal.”
2027-04-12.t: Monday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-13.a: Pope Martin I Taken Prisoner, an engraving of about 1868 from a German history of the popes. In 653 the emperor's soldiers seized Martin in the Lateran and carried him off to Constantinople for trial.
2027-04-13.b: A pope who held a council condemning an imperial heresy, he was arrested by the emperor's soldiers, tried in Constantinople and exiled to the Crimea, where he died of hunger and cold.

o.a: Pope Martin I Taken Prisoner, an engraving of about 1868 from a German history of the popes. In 653 the emperor's soldiers seized Martin in the Lateran and carried him off to Constantinople for trial.

o.t: Saint Martin I, Pope and Martyr

2027-04-13.t: Saint Martin I, Pope and Martyr

w.a: The Israelites Gathering Manna in the Desert by Nicolas Poussin, 1637–39. The starving people fall on the bread from heaven, while Moses points upward to the God who sent it. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
w.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.”
w.t: Tuesday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-14.a: The Institution of the Eucharist by Federico Barocci, 1603–08, painted for Pope Clement VIII. Christ blesses the bread among the apostles while servants bustle in the foreground. It is in Santa Maria sopra Minerva, Rome.
2027-04-14.b: “All that the Father gives me will come to me; and him who comes to me I will not cast out.”
2027-04-14.t: Wednesday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-15.a: The Last Supper by Tintoretto, 1592–94, his last great work. Christ gives the bread to the apostles in a dark inn lit by his own halo and by ghostly angels. It is in San Giorgio Maggiore, Venice.
2027-04-15.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who believes has eternal life.”
2027-04-15.t: Thursday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-16.a: The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the central panel of the Ghent Altarpiece by Hubert and Jan van Eyck, completed 1432. The Lamb of God stands on an altar, his blood flowing into a chalice, worshiped by saints from the four corners of the world. It is in St. Bavo's Cathedral, Ghent.
2027-04-16.b: “For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.”
2027-04-16.t: Friday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-17.a: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1614. 'Master, to whom shall we go?' It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-04-17.b: “We have believed, and have come to know, that you are the Holy One of God.”
2027-04-17.t: Saturday of the third week of Easter

2027-04-18.a: The Good Shepherd by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1660, showing Christ as a gentle child shepherd with his hand on a lamb, ruined columns behind him. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.
2027-04-18.b: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”

2027-04-19.a: The Good Shepherd, a mosaic of about 425–450 in the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia, Ravenna, one of the oldest and best-preserved Christian mosaics. A young, golden-robed Christ sits among his sheep beneath a deep blue vault of stars. 'I am the good shepherd.'
2027-04-19.b: “I am the door; if any one enters by me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture.”
2027-04-19.t: Monday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-20.a: The Good Shepherd by Bernhard Plockhorst, a German painter, about 1880, one of the most reproduced religious pictures of its time. Christ carries a lamb and leads the flock across a stream.
2027-04-20.t: Tuesday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-21.a: A ceiling painting by Josef Ferdinand Fromiller in the abbey church of Ossiach in Carinthia, Austria, from the 1740s. The Virgin Mary appears to Anselm in a burst of heavenly light.
2027-04-21.b: An Italian-born monk of Normandy who became Archbishop of Canterbury and was twice exiled for defending the Church against kings. His motto, 'faith seeking understanding', made him a father of scholastic theology.

2027-04-21.t: Saint Anselm, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

w.a: Christ as 'The Light of the World' by Paris Bordone, the Venetian painter who trained with Titian. It is in the National Gallery, London.
w.b: “I have come as light into the world, that whoever believes in me may not remain in darkness.”
w.t: Wednesday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-22.a: Jesus Washing Peter's Feet by Ford Madox Brown, 1852–56. Christ kneels with the towel as Peter, embarrassed, draws back his foot. It is in Tate Britain, London.
2027-04-22.b: “If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.”
2027-04-22.t: Thursday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-23.a: Saint George and the Dragon by Raphael, about 1506. George wears the Order of the Garter below his knee, perhaps because the picture was a gift for King Henry VII of England. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-04-23.b: A soldier martyred under Diocletian, honored in East and West. The legend of his slaying the dragon made him the model of the Christian knight; he is patron of England.

o.a: Saint George and the Dragon by Raphael, about 1506. George wears the Order of the Garter below his knee, perhaps because the picture was a gift for King Henry VII of England. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
o.b: A soldier martyred under Diocletian, honored in East and West. The legend of his slaying the dragon made him the model of the Christian knight; he is patron of England.

o.a: The Death of Saint Adalbert, from the bronze doors of Gniezno Cathedral, cast around 1175. Eighteen scenes tell his life, from birth to his killing by the pagan Prussians and the ransom of his body for its weight in gold. They are among the great works of Romanesque art.
o.b: A Czech nobleman who became Bishop of Prague, he left his troubled see to preach the Gospel to the pagan Prussians on the Baltic coast. He was killed there, and is a patron of Bohemia and Poland.

w.a: The Last Supper by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1480, painted on the refectory wall of the Ognissanti friary in Florence. Judas sits alone on the near side of the table; beyond the apostles, birds fly among the trees of a garden.
w.b: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father, but by me.”
w.t: Friday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-24.a: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen and Saint Joseph of Leonessa by Giambattista Tiepolo, 1752–58. Both were Capuchin friars and missionaries; Fidelis was killed preaching in Switzerland. It is in the Galleria Nazionale, Parma.
2027-04-24.b: A lawyer who became a Capuchin friar, known as the 'poor man's lawyer'. He was killed while preaching in Switzerland during the wars of religion.

o.a: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen and Saint Joseph of Leonessa by Giambattista Tiepolo, 1752–58. Both were Capuchin friars and missionaries; Fidelis was killed preaching in Switzerland. It is in the Galleria Nazionale, Parma.
o.b: A lawyer who became a Capuchin friar, known as the 'poor man's lawyer'. He was killed while preaching in Switzerland during the wars of religion.
o.t: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen, Priest and Martyr

2027-04-24.t: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen, Priest and Martyr

w.a: The Holy Trinity by El Greco, 1577–79, painted for the high altar of the monastery of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo. God the Father holds the body of his Son, with the Holy Spirit as a dove above them. It is in the Prado, Madrid.
w.b: “He who has seen me has seen the Father.”
w.t: Saturday of the fourth week of Easter

2027-04-25.a: Christ the True Vine, an icon of the 1500s, of a type first painted in Crete. Christ sits in the trunk of a vine whose branches hold the twelve apostles: 'I am the vine, you are the branches.' It is in the Byzantine and Christian Museum, Athens.
2027-04-25.b: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in me, and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.”

2027-04-26.a: Pentecost by Titian, about 1555. The Spirit descends on Mary and the apostles under a great coffered vault. It is in Santa Maria della Salute, Venice.
2027-04-26.b: “But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.”
2027-04-26.t: Monday of the fifth week of Easter

2027-04-27.a: Christ Appearing to the Apostles after the Resurrection by Szymon Czechowicz, an 18th-century Polish painter trained in Rome. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.
2027-04-27.b: “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.”
2027-04-27.t: Tuesday of the fifth week of Easter

2027-04-28.a: Peter Chanel as a young man, from his 1885 biography. He became the first martyr of Oceania, killed on the island of Futuna in 1841; within a year the island was Christian.
2027-04-28.b: A French Marist missionary to Futuna in the Pacific, killed there; the whole island soon became Christian. He is the first martyr of Oceania.

o.t: Saint Peter Chanel, Priest and Martyr

o.a: Louis de Montfort, a late 19th-century portrait. His book True Devotion to Mary was lost for over a century and found in a chest in 1842; John Paul II took his motto 'Totus tuus' from it.
o.b: A French missionary preacher whose True Devotion to Mary taught total consecration to Jesus through Mary.
o.t: Saint Louis Grignion de Montfort, Priest

2027-04-28.t: Saint Peter Chanel, Priest and Martyr

w.a: Christ the Vine, an icon from Asia Minor, 1800s. Christ sits at the root of the vine, and its branches hold the apostles. It is in the Byzantine and Christian Museum, Athens.
w.b: “By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit, and so prove to be my disciples.”
w.t: Wednesday of the fifth week of Easter

2027-04-29.a: The Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Siena by Fra Bartolomeo, 1511, painted for San Marco in Florence and given to the French ambassador. The Christ Child places a ring on her finger. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-04-29.b: A Dominican laywoman and mystic who cared for the sick and urged the pope to return from Avignon to Rome. She is a Doctor of the Church and patron of Italy and Europe.
2027-04-29.t: Saint Catherine of Siena, Virgin and Doctor of the Church

2027-04-30.a: Pope Pius V in Benediction, by a follower of Bartolomeo Passarotti, 16th century. The Dominican pope always wore his white friar's habit—which is why popes still dress in white.
2027-04-30.b: A Dominican pope who carried out the reforms of the Council of Trent, issued the Roman Missal and Catechism, and called Christendom to pray the Rosary before Lepanto.

w.a: The Last Supper by Andrea del Castagno, about 1447, on the refectory wall of the convent of Sant'Apollonia in Florence. Christ sits among his friends in a marble-panelled room, with Judas alone on the near side of the table.
w.b: “You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit and that your fruit should abide.”
w.t: Friday of the fifth week of Easter

2027-05-01.a: Saint Joseph the Carpenter by Georges de La Tour, about 1642. The boy Jesus holds a candle for Joseph as he bores into a beam that foreshadows the cross. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-05-01.b: A feast of St. Joseph the carpenter, set on May Day in 1955 to honor the dignity of human work. Jesus himself was known as 'the carpenter's son.'
