w.a: The Mocking of Christ by Fra Angelico, about 1440, painted in a friar's cell at San Marco in Florence. Christ sits blindfolded while hands strike him, and Mary and Saint Dominic keep watch in front.
w.b: “If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before it hated you.”
w.t: Saturday of the fifth week of Easter

2027-05-02.a: The Last Supper by Juan de Juanes, about 1562, the most famous of Valencia's Renaissance painters. Christ holds up the host as the apostles gather close; Judas, in the foreground, clutches the purse. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.
2027-05-02.b: “Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.”

2027-05-03.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Philip by Jusepe de Ribera, 1639. Men strain to hoist the apostle onto his cross as the crowd watches. For two centuries it was thought to show St. Bartholomew. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-05-03.b: Philip of Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus and asked, 'Show us the Father,' and James, son of Alphaeus, often identified with the leader of the Church in Jerusalem.

2027-05-04.a: The Ascension by Rembrandt, 1636, one of his Passion series for the Prince of Orange. Christ rises in a blaze of light on a cloud borne by cherubs. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.
2027-05-04.b: “Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Counselor will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.”
2027-05-04.t: Tuesday of the sixth week of Easter

2027-05-05.a: Pentecost, an 11th-century mosaic in the monastery of Hosios Loukas, Greece. Rays from the dome descend on the apostles, seated in a circle.
2027-05-05.b: “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak on his own authority, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are to come.”
2027-05-05.t: Wednesday of the sixth week of Easter

2027-05-06.a: Christ Taking Leave of the Apostles, two panels by Duccio from the back of his Maestà altarpiece for Siena Cathedral, 1308–11. At the Last Supper Christ tells them, 'A little while and you will no longer see me.' It is in the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Siena.
2027-05-06.b: “Truly, truly, I say to you, you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.”
2027-05-06.t: Thursday of the sixth week of Easter

2027-05-07.a: The Nativity at Night by Geertgen tot Sint Jans, about 1490 — the grief of labor turned to joy. The newborn Child is the only source of light in the dark stable. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-05-07.b: “So you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.”
2027-05-07.by: After Hugo van der Goes / Geertgen tot Sint Jans
2027-05-07.t: Friday of the sixth week of Easter

2027-05-08.a: Christ in Gethsemane by Heinrich Hofmann, 1890. It is in the Riverside Church, New York.
2027-05-08.b: “Hitherto you have asked nothing in my name; ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.”
2027-05-08.t: Saturday of the sixth week of Easter

2027-05-09.a: The Ascension of Christ by Pietro Perugino, about 1495–98, painted for the Benedictine abbey of San Pietro in Perugia. The apostles and Mary look up as Christ rises in a ring of angels. It was taken by Napoleon's armies and is now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Lyon.
2027-05-09.b: Forty days after Easter, the risen Christ was taken up into heaven before the eyes of his apostles, promising to send the Holy Spirit and to come again.

2027-05-10.a: Father Damien, photographed by William Brigham at Kalaupapa in 1889, weeks before he died of leprosy. He had lived among the patients of Molokai for sixteen years, and his face shows the disease he caught serving them.
2027-05-10.b: A Belgian priest who volunteered to serve the leper colony on Molokaʻi, Hawaii. He built homes, a church and a community there, and died of leprosy himself.

o.a: Portrait of Juan de Ávila from the workshop of El Greco, about 1580. It is in the El Greco Museum, Toledo.
o.b: A Spanish priest and preacher, adviser to saints such as Teresa of Ávila and John of God. Declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
o.t: Saint John of Ávila, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: The Agony in the Garden by Andrea Mantegna, about 1455. Christ prays on a rock while his disciples sleep, and Judas leads the soldiers out of Jerusalem toward them. It is in the National Gallery, London.
w.b: “In the world you have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.”
w.t: Monday of the seventh week of Easter

2027-05-11.a: The Agony in the Garden by El Greco, about 1590–95. Christ prays, his face turned to heaven, while an angel brings the cup and the apostles sleep in a cave of cloud. It is in the Toledo Museum of Art, Ohio.
2027-05-11.b: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son that the Son may glorify you.”
2027-05-11.t: Tuesday of the seventh week of Easter

2027-05-12.a: Saints Domitilla, Nereus and Achilleus by Peter Paul Rubens, 1608, painted on slate for the high altar of the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, where it still hangs. Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers who became Christians and were martyred.
2027-05-12.b: Roman soldiers who, according to an early inscription, laid down their arms on becoming Christians and were martyred.

o.a: The San Pancrazio Polyptych by Bernardo Daddi, about 1336–40, painted for the church of San Pancrazio in Florence. The boy martyr Pancras, only fourteen, stands among the saints beside the Virgin. It is in the Uffizi, Florence.
o.b: A boy of fourteen martyred in Rome under Diocletian. Churches dedicated to him, including in London, spread his name widely.

w.a: The Last Supper by Giotto, about 1305, in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. The apostles sit around the table in a simple room, John leaning on Jesus' breast.
w.b: “And for their sake I consecrate myself, that they also may be consecrated in truth.”
w.t: Wednesday of the seventh week of Easter

2027-05-13.a: Our Lady of Fátima, as she is honored at the shrine in Portugal where she appeared to three shepherd children in 1917. The crown of the shrine's statue holds the bullet that struck John Paul II in 1981.
2027-05-13.b: In 1917 the Virgin Mary appeared six times to three shepherd children at Fátima, Portugal, calling for prayer of the Rosary and conversion.

o.a: Our Lady of Fátima, as she is honored at the shrine in Portugal where she appeared to three shepherd children in 1917. The crown of the shrine's statue holds the bullet that struck John Paul II in 1981.

w.a: The Last Supper by Domenico Ghirlandaio and his brother Davide, 1476, in the refectory of the abbey of Passignano in Tuscany. The apostles sit along one side of a long white table, with Judas alone in front.
w.b: “I do not pray for these only, but also for those who believe in me through their word, that they may all be one.”
w.t: Thursday of the seventh week of Easter

2027-05-14.a: Saint Matthias by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1611, from his series of the apostles. He holds the axe of his martyrdom. The series is in the Prado, Madrid.
2027-05-14.b: Chosen by lot after the Ascension to take the place of Judas among the Twelve. Tradition holds that he preached and died a martyr.

2027-05-15.a: Saint Isidore: the Blessing of Work, by Marcello Bacciarelli, 1805, court painter to the last King of Poland. Legend says angels drove the plow while Isidore prayed. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.
2027-05-15.b: A farm laborer near Madrid, devoted to daily Mass and to the poor. Legend says angels ploughed his fields while he prayed. He is patron of farmers.

w.a: Saint John the Evangelist on Patmos by Titian and his workshop, about 1553–55, painted for a ceiling in Venice and meant to be seen from below. The beloved disciple looks up into the heavens as an eagle spreads its wings beside him. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
w.b: “If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me!”
w.t: Saturday of the seventh week of Easter

2027-05-16.a: Pentecost by El Greco, about 1600, one of his last great altarpieces. Flames burn above the apostles' heads around Mary at the center; the bald man looking out at upper right may be El Greco himself. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-05-16.b: Fifty days after Easter, the Holy Spirit descends on the apostles and Mary as tongues of fire, and they go out to preach in every language. It is the birthday of the Church.

2027-05-17.a: Pentecost by Juan Bautista Maíno, 1615–20, painted for a convent in Toledo. Mary sits at the center of the apostles as the Spirit descends—the Church gathered around her. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-05-17.b: The Monday after Pentecost honors Mary, who prayed with the apostles in the upper room as the Church was born, as Mother of the whole Church.
2027-05-17.t: Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church

2027-05-18.a: Pope John I, a chromolithograph from 1879, one of a series of portraits of all the popes from St. Peter to Leo XIII. No real likeness of him survives.
2027-05-18.b: A Tuscan who became pope and was sent by the Arian Ostrogoth king Theodoric on a mission to Constantinople. On his return the king threw him into prison at Ravenna, where he died.

2027-05-18.t: Saint John I, Pope and Martyr

w.a: Suffer the Little Children to Come unto Me by Fritz von Uhde, 1884. Christ sits in a plain room of the artist's own day, and shy village children come up to him. It is in the Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig.
w.b: “Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me, receives not me but him who sent me.”
w.t: Tuesday of the seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-19.a: An Ethiopian triptych of the 15th century: Mary and her Son in the center, the apostles and saints on the wings. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
2027-05-19.b: “For he that is not against us is for us.”
2027-05-19.t: Wednesday of the seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-20.a: Saint Bernardino of Siena Venerating the Crucifix, by Jacopo Bellini, about 1450–55, painted within a few years of the preacher's death. Jacopo was the father of Gentile and Giovanni Bellini. It is now in the United States.
2027-05-20.b: A Franciscan preacher who walked the length of Italy calling people to conversion. He spread devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, often showing the letters IHS on a tablet.

w.a: Giving Drink to the Thirsty, one panel of the Seven Works of Mercy by the Master of Alkmaar, 1504. Townspeople fill the cups of beggars and cripples while Christ stands among the poor. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
w.b: “Salt is good; but if the salt has lost its saltness, how will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
w.t: Thursday of the seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-21.a: Father Cristóbal Magallanes, shot in 1927 during the Cristero persecution in Mexico. He forgave his executioners before he died.
2027-05-21.b: A Mexican parish priest shot during the Cristero persecution after absolving his executioners. He is honored with twenty-four companions, priests and lay people.

o.a: Father Cristóbal Magallanes, shot in 1927 during the Cristero persecution in Mexico. He forgave his executioners before he died.
o.b: A Mexican parish priest shot during the Cristero persecution after absolving his executioners. He is honored with twenty-four companions, priests and lay people.
o.t: Saint Christopher Magallanes, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

2027-05-21.t: Saint Christopher Magallanes, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

w.a: Adam and Eve by Lucas Cranach the Elder, 1526. The first man and woman stand together in the garden among the animals of creation. It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
w.b: “What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder.”
w.t: Friday of the seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-22.a: Saint Rita of Cascia by Antonio de Torres, Mexico, about 1720. Rita bears the wound of a thorn on her forehead, received while praying before a crucifix. It is in the El Paso Museum of Art.
2027-05-22.b: Wife, mother and widow who became an Augustinian nun at Cascia. She is invoked as patron of impossible causes.

o.a: Saint Rita of Cascia by Antonio de Torres, Mexico, about 1720. Rita bears the wound of a thorn on her forehead, received while praying before a crucifix. It is in the El Paso Museum of Art.
o.b: Wife, mother and widow who became an Augustinian nun at Cascia. She is invoked as patron of impossible causes.

w.a: Christ Blessing the Children by Lucas Cranach the Younger and his workshop, about 1545. Mothers press forward with their babies as Christ lays his hands on them. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
w.b: “Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it.”
w.by: Lucas Cranach the Younger and workshop
w.t: Saturday of the seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-23.a: The Trinity by Andrei Rublev, about 1411–25, the most celebrated of all Russian icons. The three angels who visited Abraham sit around a table, a figure of Father, Son and Spirit in silent communion. It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
2027-05-23.b: A feast of the central mystery of the faith: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It is kept on the Sunday after Pentecost.

2027-05-24.a: Christ Counsels the Rich Young Man, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. The young man, richly dressed, stands before Christ and the apostles. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-05-24.b: “With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”
2027-05-24.t: Monday of the eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-25.a: The Last Chapter by James Doyle Penrose, an English painter of the early 1900s. It shows the story told by Bede's student Cuthbert: dying, Bede dictated the last words of his translation of St. John's Gospel, then sang 'Glory be' and died.
2027-05-25.b: A monk of Jarrow in northern England who spent his life studying, teaching and writing. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People earned him the title 'Father of English History'.

o.a: The Last Chapter by James Doyle Penrose, an English painter of the early 1900s. It shows the story told by Bede's student Cuthbert: dying, Bede dictated the last words of his translation of St. John's Gospel, then sang 'Glory be' and died.
o.b: A monk of Jarrow in northern England who spent his life studying, teaching and writing. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People earned him the title 'Father of English History'.
o.t: Saint Bede the Venerable, Priest and Doctor of the Church

o.a: Pope Gregory VII Protecting the Envoy Orlando of Parma by Francesco Hayez, 1857. Henry IV's messenger brought a letter deposing the pope, and the Roman synod nearly killed him; Gregory shielded him. Hayez was the leading painter of Romantic Italy.
o.b: Hildebrand, a monk who became pope in 1073, fought to free the Church from control by kings and to reform the clergy. He famously made the emperor Henry IV wait in the snow at Canossa.

o.a: Saint Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi Crowned with Thorns by Marcos da Cruz, about 1675. The Florentine Carmelite mystic receives Christ's crown in a vision. It is in the National Museum of Ancient Art, Lisbon.
o.b: A Carmelite nun of Florence known for her ecstasies and her prayer for the renewal of the Church.
o.t: Saint Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi, Virgin

2027-05-25.t: Saint Bede the Venerable, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: The Calling of Saints Peter and Andrew, attributed to Caravaggio, about 1603–06. Christ calls the two fishermen brothers away from their work. It is in the Royal Collection, at Hampton Court Palace.
w.b: “But many that are first will be last, and the last first.”
w.t: Tuesday of the eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-26.a: Saint Philip Neri by Carlo Dolci, 1645–46. The joyful founder of the Oratory was known as the Apostle of Rome. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-05-26.b: The 'Apostle of Rome', known for his joy and humor. He founded the Oratory, where prayer, music and conversation brought many back to faith.

2027-05-27.a: Augustine Preaching Before King Ethelbert, by James Doyle, from A Chronicle of England, 1864, printed in color by Edmund Evans. The king of Kent listens to the monks from Rome in the open air, wary of their magic indoors.
2027-05-27.b: A Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to the English. He baptized King Ethelbert of Kent and became the first Archbishop of Canterbury.
2027-05-27.by: James William Edmund Doyle / Edmund Evans

o.b: A Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to the English. He baptized King Ethelbert of Kent and became the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

w.a: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Venice. Christ touches the eyes of the blind man in a deep Venetian piazza. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
w.b: “Go your way; your faith has made you well.”
w.t: Thursday of the eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-28.a: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple by Hubert Robert, 1760, the French painter of ruins and grand architecture. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-05-28.b: “Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you receive it, and you will.”
2027-05-28.t: Friday of the eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-29.a: Pope Paul VI, an official portrait of 1969. He completed the Second Vatican Council and was the first pope to fly in an airplane and visit five continents.
2027-05-29.b: Giovanni Battista Montini, pope from 1963 to 1978, who brought the Second Vatican Council to completion and was the first pope to travel by plane to five continents.

o.a: Pope Paul VI, an official portrait of 1969. He completed the Second Vatican Council and was the first pope to fly in an airplane and visit five continents.
o.b: Giovanni Battista Montini, pope from 1963 to 1978, who brought the Second Vatican Council to completion and was the first pope to travel by plane to five continents.

w.a: The Expulsion of the Money-changers from the Temple by Giotto, about 1305, in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. The next day the priests and elders came to ask him by what authority he had done it.
w.b: “By what authority are you doing these things, or who gave you this authority to do them?”
w.t: Saturday of the eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-05-30.a: The Disputation of the Holy Sacrament by Raphael, 1509–10, in the Vatican's Stanza della Segnatura. Heaven and earth meet at the monstrance on the altar: the Trinity and saints above, popes, theologians and Dante below.
2027-05-30.b: Corpus Christi, a feast of the Eucharist, in which Christ gives his body and blood under the forms of bread and wine. It is traditionally marked by processions through the streets.
2027-05-30.by: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
2027-05-30.t: The Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ

2027-05-31.a: The Visitation by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1491. Elizabeth kneels before Mary under a classical arch, as Mary Jacobi and Mary Salome look on. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-05-31.b: Mary hurries to visit her cousin Elizabeth, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy. Mary answers with her great hymn of praise, the Magnificat.
2027-05-31.t: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-06-01.a: Saint Justin the Philosopher by Theophanes the Cretan, about 1546, on Mount Athos. Justin is shown with a scroll, as the first great Christian philosopher.
2027-06-01.b: A philosopher who found in Christianity 'the only sure and useful philosophy'. His writings defended the faith to the emperor, and he was beheaded in Rome.

2027-06-02.a: Saint Marcellinus, from Seligenstadt, Germany. In 827 Charlemagne's biographer Einhard brought the relics of Marcellinus and Peter from Rome to Seligenstadt, where they still rest in the basilica he built.
2027-06-02.b: A priest and an exorcist of Rome, martyred under Diocletian. Their names are recalled in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

o.a: Saint Marcellinus, from Seligenstadt, Germany. In 827 Charlemagne's biographer Einhard brought the relics of Marcellinus and Peter from Rome to Seligenstadt, where they still rest in the basilica he built.
o.b: A priest and an exorcist of Rome, martyred under Diocletian. Their names are recalled in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

w.a: Moses before the Burning Bush by Domenico Fetti. Moses kneels before the fire from which God speaks: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.
w.b: “He is not God of the dead, but of the living.”
w.t: Wednesday of the ninth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-03.a: The Basilica of the Uganda Martyrs at Namugongo, built in the shape of a traditional Ganda hut over the place where Charles Lwanga was burned to death in 1886. Every June 3, more than a million pilgrims walk there, many of them for days, from across East Africa.
2027-06-03.b: Charles Lwanga, head of the royal pages of Buganda, protected the young pages in his care and was burned alive at Namugongo with Catholic and Anglican companions.
2027-06-03.t: Saints Charles Lwanga and Companions, Martyrs

2027-06-04.a: The Sacred Heart of Jesus by Pompeo Batoni, 1767, painted for the Church of the Gesù in Rome, where it hangs. It became the model for countless devotional images of the Sacred Heart around the world.
2027-06-04.b: The heart of Christ, pierced on the cross, as the sign of his love for all people. 'Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened.'
2027-06-04.t: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus

2027-06-05.a: The Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary by Vicente López Portaña, about 1830, court painter to the Spanish kings. It is in the Diocesan Museum of Sacred Art in Orihuela, Spain.
2027-06-05.b: The day after the feast of the Sacred Heart, the Church honors the heart of Mary, who 'kept all these things, pondering them in her heart.'
2027-06-05.t: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-06-06.a: Jesus Preaching to the Multitude by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Crowds press around Jesus to listen, as they did in the house at Capernaum.
2027-06-06.b: “Whoever does the will of God is my brother, and sister, and mother.”

2027-06-07.a: The Sermon on the Mount by Jan Brueghel the Elder, 1598, painted on copper. A huge crowd in Flemish dress gathers on a hillside to hear Christ. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.
2027-06-07.b: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.”
2027-06-07.t: Monday of the tenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-08.a: The Sermon on the Mount by Carl Bloch, 1877, one of 23 Gospel scenes he painted for the chapel of Frederiksborg Castle, Denmark.
2027-06-08.b: “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.”
2027-06-08.t: Tuesday of the tenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-09.a: The Death of Ephrem the Syrian, a Cretan icon by Emmanuel Tzanfournaris, 17th century. Monks and hermits from across the desert gather around the body of the poet-saint. It is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.
2027-06-09.b: A deacon of Nisibis and Edessa, called the 'Harp of the Spirit' for his hymns and poetry. A Doctor of the Church.

o.a: The Death of Ephrem the Syrian, a Cretan icon by Emmanuel Tzanfournaris, 17th century. Monks and hermits from across the desert gather around the body of the poet-saint. It is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.
o.b: A deacon of Nisibis and Edessa, called the 'Harp of the Spirit' for his hymns and poetry. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Ephrem, Deacon and Doctor of the Church

2027-06-09.t: Saint Ephrem, Deacon and Doctor of the Church

w.a: Moses with the Ten Commandments by Philippe de Champaigne, about 1648. Moses holds up the two tablets of the law, with light streaming from his head.
w.b: “For truly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, not an iota, not a dot, will pass from the law until all is accomplished.”
w.t: Wednesday of the tenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-10.a: The Reconciliation of Jacob and Esau, 17th century, Flemish. The brothers embrace after twenty years of enmity — 'go first and be reconciled with your brother.' It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-06-10.b: “For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.”
2027-06-10.t: Thursday of the tenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-11.a: Paul and Barnabas at Lystra by Pieter Lastman, Rembrandt's teacher, 1617. After a healing, the crowd takes the apostles for the gods Zeus and Hermes and tries to sacrifice an ox to them; the apostles tear their clothes in protest. It is in the Amsterdam Museum.
2027-06-11.b: A Cypriot Jew whose name means 'son of encouragement', he vouched for the newly converted Paul and travelled with him on the first missionary journey. Tradition says he was martyred on Cyprus.

2027-06-12.a: The Sermon on the Mount by Fra Angelico, about 1440–42, painted on the wall of a friar's cell at the Convent of San Marco, Florence. The apostles sit in a ring on the bare rock around Christ.
2027-06-12.b: “Let what you say be simply ‘Yes’ or ‘No’; anything more than this comes from evil.”
2027-06-12.t: Saturday of the tenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-13.a: Head of Christ by Rembrandt, about 1648–56, one of a series of small studies he painted from a young Jewish man of Amsterdam. Gentle and searching, it broke with centuries of idealized portraits of Jesus. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
2027-06-13.b: “It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth; yet when it is sown it grows up and becomes the greatest of all shrubs.”

2027-06-14.a: The Mocking of Christ by Fra Angelico, 1440–41, in cell 7 of the Convent of San Marco, Florence. Blindfolded, Christ sits calmly while disembodied hands strike him and a head spits; below, Mary and St. Dominic meditate.
2027-06-14.b: “But I say to you, Do not resist one who is evil. But if any one strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.”
2027-06-14.t: Monday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-15.a: The Good Samaritan by Théodule Ribot, 1870, a French realist known for his dark, Spanish-inspired style. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Pau.
2027-06-15.b: “You, therefore, must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”
2027-06-15.t: Tuesday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-16.a: An Old Woman Praying by Nicolaes Maes, about 1655, a pupil of Rembrandt. Alone at her table, among her Bible, hourglass and skull, she prays with folded hands.
2027-06-16.b: “But when you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
2027-06-16.t: Wednesday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-17.a: The Angelus by Jean-François Millet, 1857–59. At the sound of the distant church bell, two peasants stop work in the field to pray. It is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
2027-06-17.b: “Pray then like this: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done, On earth as it is in heaven.”
2027-06-17.t: Thursday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-18.a: The Parable of the Rich Fool by Rembrandt, 1627, painted when he was 21. An old man examines a coin by candlelight among his ledgers and money bags. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-06-18.b: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.”
2027-06-18.t: Friday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-19.a: Saint Romuald by Fra Angelico, about 1440, a small panel from the high altarpiece of San Marco in Florence. The founder of the Camaldolese hermits wears their white habit. It is in the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
2027-06-19.b: A nobleman of Ravenna who became a monk and founded the Camaldolese, uniting the hermit's life with community.

o.a: Saint Romuald by Fra Angelico, about 1440, a small panel from the high altarpiece of San Marco in Florence. The founder of the Camaldolese hermits wears their white habit. It is in the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
o.b: A nobleman of Ravenna who became a monk and founded the Camaldolese, uniting the hermit's life with community.

w.a: Saint Francis Preaching to the Birds, Johann Anton Ramboux's copy of the fresco in the Upper Church of San Francesco, Assisi. Francis speaks to the birds of the air, which neither sow nor reap, and yet God feeds them.
w.b: “But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be yours as well.”
w.t: Saturday of the eleventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-20.a: Christ on the Sea of Galilee by Eugène Delacroix, 1841. Waves toss the little boat as the disciples panic and Christ sleeps peacefully in the stern. Delacroix painted the subject many times. It is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.
2027-06-20.b: “Who then is this, that even wind and sea obey him?”

2027-06-21.a: The Vocation of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga by Guercino, about 1650. The young nobleman lays aside his crown and turns to the crucifix, choosing religious life over his inheritance. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-06-21.b: Born heir to a noble Italian house, he gave up his title to join the Jesuits. He died at twenty-three after nursing victims of plague in Rome, and is patron of young people.

2027-06-22.a: Sir Thomas More by Hans Holbein the Younger, 1527, painted while Holbein lived in More's household in Chelsea. More wears the gold chain of royal service he would later lose with his life. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.
2027-06-22.b: A bishop and a Lord Chancellor of England who refused to accept King Henry VIII as head of the Church. More went to his death 'the King's good servant, but God's first.'

o.a: Saint Paulinus of Nola, an 18th-century canvas in the Diocesan Museum of Caltagirone, Sicily. Paulinus, a rich Roman senator and poet, gave away his fortune to become a priest and bishop of Nola.
o.b: A wealthy Roman senator and poet who gave away his fortune with his wife, Therasia, and became bishop of Nola.

o.a: Sir Thomas More by Hans Holbein the Younger, 1527, painted while Holbein lived in More's household in Chelsea. More wears the gold chain of royal service he would later lose with his life. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.
o.b: A bishop and a Lord Chancellor of England who refused to accept King Henry VIII as head of the Church. More went to his death 'the King's good servant, but God's first.'
o.t: Saints John Fisher, Bishop, and Thomas More, Martyrs

2027-06-22.t: Saints John Fisher, Bishop, and Thomas More, Martyrs

w.a: The Broad and the Narrow Way, the English edition (1883) of a German print first published in 1866. The wide road on the left runs past theaters and taverns to destruction; the narrow one climbs past church and Sunday school to the heavenly city. It is in the British Museum.
w.b: “So whatever you wish that men would do to you, do so to them; for this is the law and the prophets.”
w.t: Tuesday of the twelfth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-23.a: The Sermon on the Mount by Claude Lorrain, 1656. Christ teaches from a wooded hill that rises out of a wide, imagined Holy Land, with the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan below. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.
2027-06-23.b: “You will know them by their fruits. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from thistles?”
2027-06-23.t: Wednesday of the twelfth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-24.a: The Birth of Saint John the Baptist by Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1486–90, in the Tornabuoni Chapel of Santa Maria Novella, Florence. Elegant Florentine ladies visit Elizabeth, as if the birth had taken place in their own city.
2027-06-24.b: The birth of John to the aged Elizabeth and Zechariah, who regained his voice to name him. One of the few saints whose birthday is celebrated, six months before Christmas.
2027-06-24.t: The Nativity of Saint John the Baptist

2027-06-25.a: Christ Heals a Leper, a Dutch drawing in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-06-25.b: “He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, ‘I will; be clean.’ And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.”
2027-06-25.t: Friday of the twelfth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-26.a: The Centurion of Capernaum by Johannes Ykens, a 17th-century Flemish painter. The Roman officer bows before Christ: 'Lord, I am not worthy.'
2027-06-26.b: “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”
2027-06-26.t: Saturday of the twelfth week of Ordinary Time

2027-06-27.a: The Raising of Jairus's Daughter by Ilya Repin, 1871, painted at twenty-seven for the gold medal of the St. Petersburg Academy, which he won. It is in the State Russian Museum.
2027-06-27.b: “Taking her by the hand he said to her, ‘Talitha cumi’; which means, ‘Little girl, I say to you, arise.’”

2027-06-28.a: A modern icon of Irenaeus of Lyon. As a boy in Asia Minor he heard St. Polycarp, who had known St. John the Apostle—a living link between the apostles and the Church in Gaul.
2027-06-28.b: A disciple of Polycarp, who had known St. John. As bishop of Lyon he wrote Against Heresies. Named a Doctor of the Church in 2022.
2027-06-28.t: Saint Irenaeus, Bishop, Martyr and Doctor of the Church

2027-06-29.a: Saint Peter and Saint Paul by El Greco, 1587–92. Gentle, downcast Peter with his keys and fiery Paul with his book—two temperaments, one faith. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.
2027-06-29.b: The fisherman whom Christ made the rock of his Church, and the persecutor who became the Apostle to the Gentiles. Both were martyred in Rome—Peter crucified upside down, Paul beheaded.

2027-06-30.a: Nero's Torches by Henryk Siemiradzki, 1876, a canvas seven meters wide. Christians are bound to stakes, about to be set alight, as the emperor arrives for the spectacle. It is in the Sukiennice gallery of the National Museum in Kraków.
2027-06-30.b: After the great fire of Rome, Nero blamed the Christians. Many were crucified, thrown to beasts or burned as living torches in his gardens—the first martyrs of the Church of Rome.

o.a: Nero's Torches by Henryk Siemiradzki, 1876, a canvas seven meters wide. Christians are bound to stakes, about to be set alight, as the emperor arrives for the spectacle. It is in the Sukiennice gallery of the National Museum in Kraków.
o.b: After the great fire of Rome, Nero blamed the Christians. Many were crucified, thrown to beasts or burned as living torches in his gardens—the first martyrs of the Church of Rome.
o.t: The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church

2027-06-30.t: The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church

w.a: The Miracle of the Gadarene Swine, a page from a manuscript painted around the year 1000. The demons driven out of the men enter the herd of swine, which rush down into the sea.
w.b: “And behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their neighborhood.”
w.t: Wednesday of the thirteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-01.a: Junípero Serra, from the 1787 biography by his companion Francisco Palóu, the earliest known likeness. He founded the first nine of California's twenty-one missions.
2027-07-01.b: A Franciscan from Majorca who founded the first nine missions of California. He was canonized in 2015.

o.a: Junípero Serra, from the 1787 biography by his companion Francisco Palóu, the earliest known likeness. He founded the first nine of California's twenty-one missions.
o.b: A Franciscan from Majorca who founded the first nine missions of California. He was canonized in 2015.

w.a: The Healing of the Paralytic at Capernaum by Belisario Corenzio, on the ceiling of the chapter room of the monastery of Santi Severino e Sossio in Naples, early 1600s.
w.b: “Take heart, my son; your sins are forgiven.”
w.t: Thursday of the thirteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-02.a: The Calling of Saint Matthew by Hendrick ter Brugghen, 1621, a Dutch follower of Caravaggio. Matthew, at a table crowded with coins and tax collectors, points to himself: 'Me?' It is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht.
2027-07-02.b: “As Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax office; and he said to him, ‘Follow me.’ And he rose and followed him.”
2027-07-02.t: Friday of the thirteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-03.a: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas by Caravaggio, about 1601–02. Christ guides Thomas's finger into the wound in his side as two apostles lean in. It is in the Sanssouci Picture Gallery, Potsdam.
2027-07-03.b: The apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection until he touched the wounds, then cried, 'My Lord and my God!' Tradition says he carried the Gospel to India.

2027-07-04.a: Christ in the Synagogue by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. Jesus teaches in the synagogue as the elders look on, as he did in his hometown of Nazareth, where they asked, 'Is he not the carpenter?'
2027-07-04.b: “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.”

2027-07-05.a: Saint Elizabeth of Portugal by Francisco de Zurbarán, about 1635. She carries roses in her skirt: legend says the bread she was secretly taking to the poor turned to roses when her husband stopped her. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-07-05.b: Queen of Portugal, known as a peacemaker within her own family and between kings. After her husband's death she lived as a Poor Clare tertiary.

o.a: Saint Elizabeth of Portugal by Francisco de Zurbarán, about 1635. She carries roses in her skirt: legend says the bread she was secretly taking to the poor turned to roses when her husband stopped her. It is in the Museo del Prado.
o.b: Queen of Portugal, known as a peacemaker within her own family and between kings. After her husband's death she lived as a Poor Clare tertiary.

o.a: Saint Anthony Zaccaria holds the rule of his Barnabites, a lily for purity and a scourge for penance. He began as a doctor in Cremona before becoming a priest.
o.b: A doctor from Cremona who became a priest and founded the Barnabites. He spread devotion to the Eucharist and to the letters of St. Paul, and died at thirty-six.

w.a: The Raising of Jairus' Daughter by Vasily Polenov, 1871, the painting that won him the gold medal of the Imperial Academy of Arts in St. Petersburg. Christ reaches toward the girl on her bed as her mother kneels and the mourners wait in the shadows.
w.b: “Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.”
w.t: Monday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-06.a: Maria Goretti by Giuseppe Brovelli-Soffredini, 1929. No photograph of her existed, so the painter worked from her mother's descriptions. Her mother lived to attend her canonization in 1950.
2027-07-06.b: An Italian farm girl of eleven who died resisting an attacker and forgave him before she died. He repented and was present at her canonization.

o.a: Maria Goretti by Giuseppe Brovelli-Soffredini, 1929. No photograph of her existed, so the painter worked from her mother's descriptions. Her mother lived to attend her canonization in 1950.
o.b: An Italian farm girl of eleven who died resisting an attacker and forgave him before she died. He repented and was present at her canonization.
o.t: Saint Maria Goretti, Virgin and Martyr

2027-07-06.t: Saint Maria Goretti, Virgin and Martyr

w.a: The Gleaners by Jean-François Millet, 1857. Three peasant women bend to pick up the ears of grain left behind, while the great harvest is gathered in the distance. It is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
w.b: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; pray therefore the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”
w.t: Tuesday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-07.a: The Sending of the Apostles, an 18th-century ceiling fresco in the monastery church of Nová Říše in Moravia.
2027-07-07.b: “Preach as you go, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven is at hand.’”
2027-07-07.t: Wednesday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-08.a: The Mission of the Apostles, 1631, in the Chapel of Saint Matthias in the Basilica of Santa Giustina, Padua.
2027-07-08.b: “Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You received without pay, give without pay.”
2027-07-08.t: Thursday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-09.a: An icon of the martyrs of the Boxer Rebellion of 1900, painted in 1990 at Holy Transfiguration Monastery in Brookline, Massachusetts. Eighty-six of the 120 Catholic martyrs of China canonized in 2000 died in that same uprising.
2027-07-09.b: Augustine Zhao Rong, a soldier who became a priest, died in prison in 1815. He is honored with 119 others, Chinese and missionary, martyred over three centuries and canonized together in 2000.

o.a: An icon of the martyrs of the Boxer Rebellion of 1900, painted in 1990 at Holy Transfiguration Monastery in Brookline, Massachusetts. Eighty-six of the 120 Catholic martyrs of China canonized in 2000 died in that same uprising.
o.b: Augustine Zhao Rong, a soldier who became a priest, died in prison in 1815. He is honored with 119 others, Chinese and missionary, martyred over three centuries and canonized together in 2000.
o.t: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

2027-07-09.t: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

w.a: The Mission of the Apostles by Battista Bissoni, 1631, in the Chapel of Saint Matthias at the abbey of Santa Giustina, Padua. Christ sends the Twelve out to preach.
w.b: “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.”
w.t: Friday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-10.a: Christus Consolator by Ary Scheffer, 1837. Christ comforts the suffering of every age — a slave, a mourning mother, a prisoner — 'Do not be afraid.' It is in the Dordrechts Museum, the Netherlands.
2027-07-10.b: “What I tell you in the dark, utter in the light; and what you hear whispered, proclaim upon the housetops.”
2027-07-10.t: Saturday of the fourteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-11.a: The Exhortation to the Apostles by James Tissot, 1886–94, from his series of 350 scenes of the life of Christ, painted after years of travel in the Holy Land. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
2027-07-11.b: “So they went out and preached that men should repent. And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many that were sick and healed them.”

2027-07-12.a: The Seven Works of Mercy by Caravaggio, 1607, painted for a charitable brotherhood in Naples. In one dark street, a man gives a drink to the thirsty, a daughter feeds her imprisoned father, and the dead are carried out. It still hangs in the Pio Monte della Misericordia, Naples.
2027-07-12.b: “Whoever gives to one of these little ones even a cup of cold water because he is a disciple, truly, I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.”
2027-07-12.t: Monday of the fifteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-13.a: The Heinrichstafel, a panel by the Master of the Legend of Saint Barbara, Brussels, about 1490. It tells the story of the emperor: his coronation in Rome, a vision of the Cross and his victory in battle.
2027-07-13.b: Holy Roman Emperor who supported church reform and founded the diocese of Bamberg, where he is buried beside his wife, St. Cunigunde.
2027-07-13.by: Master of the Legend of Saint Barbara

o.a: The Heinrichstafel, a panel by the Master of the Legend of Saint Barbara, Brussels, about 1490. It tells the story of the emperor: his coronation in Rome, a vision of the Cross and his victory in battle.
o.b: Holy Roman Emperor who supported church reform and founded the diocese of Bamberg, where he is buried beside his wife, St. Cunigunde.
o.by: Master of the Legend of Saint Barbara

w.a: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah by John Martin, 1852. Fire falls from heaven on the two cities as Lot and his daughters flee and his wife turns back. It is in the Laing Art Gallery, Newcastle.
w.b: “Woe to you, Chorazin! woe to you, Beth-saida! for if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.”
w.t: Tuesday of the fifteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-14.a: Kateri Tekakwitha, after the portrait attributed to Father Claude Chauchetière, the Jesuit who knew her at Kahnawake—the earliest known image of her, painted in the years after her death in 1680.
2027-07-14.b: A Mohawk-Algonquin woman baptized at twenty, who lived a life of prayer and penance near Montreal. The 'Lily of the Mohawks' is the first Native American saint.

2027-07-15.a: The Lying-in-State of Saint Bonaventure by Francisco de Zurbarán, 1629. He died during the Council of Lyon, and the pope and the king of Aragon came to mourn him. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-07-15.b: An Italian Franciscan who taught in Paris alongside Thomas Aquinas and led his order for seventeen years. A cardinal and Doctor of the Church, he wrote the Journey of the Mind to God.
2027-07-15.t: Saint Bonaventure, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-07-16.a: Our Lady of Mount Carmel by Onorio Marinari, 17th century, in the church of San Bartolomeo in Cutigliano, Tuscany. The Virgin and Child appear to Carmelite saints.
2027-07-16.b: Patronal feast of the Carmelites, who take their name from Mount Carmel in the Holy Land. Devotion to the brown scapular is linked to this feast.

o.a: Our Lady of Mount Carmel by Onorio Marinari, 17th century, in the church of San Bartolomeo in Cutigliano, Tuscany. The Virgin and Child appear to Carmelite saints.
o.b: Patronal feast of the Carmelites, who take their name from Mount Carmel in the Holy Land. Devotion to the brown scapular is linked to this feast.

w.a: The Disciples Plucking Grain on the Sabbath, one of the 160 panels of the Gotha Altarpiece painted in Heinrich Füllmaurer's workshop about 1538. It is at Friedenstein Castle, Gotha.
w.b: “And if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.”
w.t: Friday of the fifteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-17.a: Christ Healing the Sick by Washington Allston, 1813, the first great American painter of Bible scenes. It is in the Worcester Art Museum, Massachusetts.
2027-07-17.b: “He will not break a bruised reed or quench a smoldering wick, till he brings justice to victory.”
2027-07-17.t: Saturday of the fifteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-18.a: The Hundred Guilder Print by Rembrandt, about 1649, his most famous etching. Christ stands in the middle of a crowd of the sick, the poor and the curious, welcoming them all. Its nickname comes from the then-record price it fetched. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-07-18.b: “He said to them, ‘Come away by yourselves to a lonely place, and rest a while.’ For many were coming and going, and they had no leisure even to eat.”

2027-07-19.a: Jonah and the Whale by Pieter Lastman, 1621, Rembrandt's teacher. The great fish spits Jonah onto the shore after three days and three nights. It is in the Museum Kunstpalast, Düsseldorf.
2027-07-19.b: “For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”
2027-07-19.t: Monday of the sixteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-20.a: A detail of the 6th-century mosaic in the apse of Sant'Apollinare in Classe, near Ravenna. Apollinaris stands with arms raised in prayer among twelve lambs in a green paradise; the basilica was built over his grave.
2027-07-20.b: Remembered as the first bishop of Ravenna, he preached through repeated imprisonment and exile. The great basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe bears his name.

o.a: A detail of the 6th-century mosaic in the apse of Sant'Apollinare in Classe, near Ravenna. Apollinaris stands with arms raised in prayer among twelve lambs in a green paradise; the basilica was built over his grave.
o.b: Remembered as the first bishop of Ravenna, he preached through repeated imprisonment and exile. The great basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe bears his name.

w.a: The Holy Kinship (the Torgau Altarpiece) by Lucas Cranach the Elder, 1509. Mary and her relatives gather with their children, among them the 'brethren of the Lord'. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.
w.b: “For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, and sister, and mother.”
w.t: Tuesday of the sixteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-21.a: An altar painting of Saint Lawrence of Brindisi in the church of the Holy Spirit at Francavilla Fontana, in his native Apulia. The Capuchin preacher is shown in glory with angels.
2027-07-21.b: A Capuchin friar, preacher and diplomat who knew many languages. He led troops into battle holding only a crucifix. A Doctor of the Church.

o.a: An altar painting of Saint Lawrence of Brindisi in the church of the Holy Spirit at Francavilla Fontana, in his native Apulia. The Capuchin preacher is shown in glory with angels.
o.b: A Capuchin friar, preacher and diplomat who knew many languages. He led troops into battle holding only a crucifix. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-07-21.t: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: September: the Parable of the Sower by Marten van Valckenborch, 1580s, from a series of the months set in the Flemish countryside.
w.b: “A sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seeds fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured them.”
w.t: Wednesday of the sixteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-22.a: The Penitent Magdalene by Titian, about 1533, painted for the Duke of Urbino. She looks to heaven, wrapped only in her golden hair. Titian painted the subject many times, but this is the most celebrated. It is in the Palazzo Pitti, Florence.
2027-07-22.b: A follower of Jesus from Galilee, freed by him from seven demons, who stood by the cross and was first to see him risen. She is called 'the apostle to the apostles.'

2027-07-23.a: Saint Bridget of Sweden by the Florentine painter Maso da San Friano, from the mid-1500s. Bridget spent her last twenty-four years in Italy, where her Revelations were widely read. It is in the York Art Gallery, England.
2027-07-23.b: A Swedish noblewoman, mother of eight, whose visions and counsel reached popes and kings. She founded the Bridgettines and is a patron of Europe.

o.a: Saint Bridget of Sweden by the Florentine painter Maso da San Friano, from the mid-1500s. Bridget spent her last twenty-four years in Italy, where her Revelations were widely read. It is in the York Art Gallery, England.
o.b: A Swedish noblewoman, mother of eight, whose visions and counsel reached popes and kings. She founded the Bridgettines and is a patron of Europe.

w.a: The Sower by Vincent van Gogh, June 1888, painted at Arles. A sower strides across a violet field under a huge yellow sun, with ripe wheat behind him. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.
w.b: “As for what was sown on good soil, this is he who hears the word and understands it; he indeed bears fruit, and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty.”
w.t: Friday of the sixteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-24.a: The traditional image of Saint Charbel, his face shadowed by his monk's hood. No photograph from his lifetime is known; this face became famous after a photograph taken at his monastery of Annaya in 1950.
2027-07-24.b: A Lebanese Maronite monk and hermit who lived in silence and prayer for twenty-three years. Countless healings have been attributed to his intercession.

w.a: The Parable of the Wheat and the Tares by Domenico Fetti, one of his small parable paintings made in Mantua around 1620. While everyone sleeps, the enemy sows weeds among the wheat. It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
w.b: “Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.”
w.t: Saturday of the sixteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-25.a: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1545–50. The crowd spreads across a wide landscape as the bread is passed out. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-07-25.b: “There is a lad here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are they among so many?”

2027-07-26.a: The Meeting of Joachim and Anne at the Golden Gate by Filippino Lippi, 1497. Told separately by angels that they would have a child, the elderly couple embrace at the gate of Jerusalem. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.
2027-07-26.b: According to ancient tradition, the parents of the Virgin Mary and grandparents of Jesus. They are honored together as patrons of grandparents.
2027-07-26.t: Saints Joachim and Anne, Parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-07-27.a: Landscape with the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares by Abraham Bloemaert, 1624. While the farmhands sleep, the devil slips through the field sowing weeds. It is in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
2027-07-27.b: “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.”
2027-07-27.t: Tuesday of the seventeenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-28.a: The Parable of the Hidden Treasure, from the workshop of Rembrandt, about 1630, possibly painted with his first pupil Gerard Dou. A man digs by night in the field where the treasure lies. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.
2027-07-28.b: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up; then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.”
2027-07-28.t: Wednesday of the seventeenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-29.a: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary by Johannes Vermeer, about 1654–55, his largest painting and one of his very few religious scenes. Martha sets down the bread as Mary listens at Jesus's feet. It is in the Scottish National Gallery, Edinburgh.
2027-07-29.b: Friends of Jesus who welcomed him into their home at Bethany: busy Martha, Mary who sat at his feet, and Lazarus, whom Jesus wept for and raised from the dead.

2027-07-30.a: Saints Peter Chrysologus, Romuald and Peter Damian, by Giuseppe Milani, in the Cathedral of Ravenna. Three saints of Ravenna together: its great bishop, its hermit and its reformer.
2027-07-30.b: Bishop of Ravenna, whose short, vivid sermons earned him the name 'Golden Word'. A Doctor of the Church.

o.a: Saints Peter Chrysologus, Romuald and Peter Damian, by Giuseppe Milani, in the Cathedral of Ravenna. Three saints of Ravenna together: its great bishop, its hermit and its reformer.
o.b: Bishop of Ravenna, whose short, vivid sermons earned him the name 'Golden Word'. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Peter Chrysologus, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-07-30.t: Saint Peter Chrysologus, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

w.a: The Childhood of Christ by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. By candlelight the boy Jesus holds the light for Joseph at his carpenter's bench. It is in the Hermitage, St. Petersburg.
w.b: “Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary?”
w.t: Friday of the seventeenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-07-31.a: The Miracles of Saint Ignatius of Loyola by Peter Paul Rubens, 1617–18, painted for the high altar of the new Jesuit church in Antwerp. Ignatius drives out demons and heals the sick. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-07-31.b: A Basque soldier converted while recovering from a cannonball wound. He wrote the Spiritual Exercises and founded the Society of Jesus, the Jesuits.

2027-08-01.a: The Saviour with the Eucharist by Juan de Juanes, about 1545–50, once the door of the tabernacle on a Valencian high altar. Christ holds up the host and chalice. It is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.
2027-08-01.b: “I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger, and he who believes in me shall never thirst.”

2027-08-02.a: The Virgin in Glory with the Archangel Gabriel and Saints Eusebius, Sebastian and Roch, by Sebastiano Ricci, 1724–25, one of the last works of the Venetian painter. It belongs to the University of Turin.
2027-08-02.b: First bishop of Vercelli, he lived in community with his clergy and suffered exile for defending the Nicene faith against the Arians.

o.a: The Virgin in Glory with the Archangel Gabriel and Saints Eusebius, Sebastian and Roch, by Sebastiano Ricci, 1724–25, one of the last works of the Venetian painter. It belongs to the University of Turin.
o.b: First bishop of Vercelli, he lived in community with his clergy and suffered exile for defending the Nicene faith against the Arians.

o.a: Saint Peter Julian Eymard, called the Apostle of the Eucharist. He founded the Blessed Sacrament Fathers in Paris to keep perpetual adoration.
o.b: A French priest devoted to the Eucharist who founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament.

w.a: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Jacopo Tintoretto, about 1545–50. The great crowd sits on the hillside as the bread and fish are handed out. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
w.b: “They need not go away; you give them something to eat.”
w.t: Monday of the eighteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-03.a: Christ at the Sea of Galilee, from the circle of Tintoretto, about 1575. Christ stands on the shore of the storm-tossed sea as Peter climbs over the side of the boat toward him. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-08-03.b: “O man of little faith, why did you doubt?”
2027-08-03.t: Tuesday of the eighteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-04.a: 'Authentic portrait of the holy Curé of Ars, made from life', a 19th-century French print of the priest of Ars in his last days. It is in the National Library of France.
2027-08-04.b: The Curé of Ars, a village priest who spent up to sixteen hours a day hearing confessions. He is patron of parish priests.

2027-08-05.a: The Founding of Santa Maria Maggiore by Masolino, about 1428. Christ and Mary send snow on an August night, and Pope Liberius traces the church's outline in it. It was the center of an altarpiece painted with Masaccio and is in the Capodimonte Museum, Naples.
2027-08-05.b: The great Roman church of Mary, rebuilt after the Council of Ephesus proclaimed her Mother of God in 431. Legend says its site was marked by a miraculous snowfall in August.

o.t: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major

2027-08-05.t: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major

w.a: Christ Giving the Keys of Heaven to Saint Peter by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1612–15. Peter kneels to receive the keys of the kingdom. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
w.b: “And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the powers of death shall not prevail against it.”
w.t: Thursday of the eighteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-06.a: The Transfiguration by Raphael, 1516–20, his last painting. Above, Christ shines on the mountain; below, the disciples struggle to heal a possessed boy. It was hung above his body at his funeral. It is in the Vatican Pinacoteca.
2027-08-06.b: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, his face shining like the sun, as Moses and Elijah appear beside him and a voice says, 'This is my beloved Son.'

2027-08-07.a: The Sistine Madonna by Raphael, about 1512, painted for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza. Pope Sixtus II kneels at left, his tiara set on the ledge; the two famous cherubs lean on the frame below. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
2027-08-07.b: Pope Sixtus was seized while celebrating Mass in the catacombs and beheaded with four of his deacons. His deacon Lawrence followed days later.

o.a: The Sistine Madonna by Raphael, about 1512, painted for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza. Pope Sixtus II kneels at left, his tiara set on the ledge; the two famous cherubs lean on the frame below. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
o.b: Pope Sixtus was seized while celebrating Mass in the catacombs and beheaded with four of his deacons. His deacon Lawrence followed days later.
o.t: Saint Sixtus II, Pope, and Companions, Martyrs

o.a: Saint Cajetan's Vision of the Holy Family by Giambattista Tiepolo, about 1735. On Christmas night in Rome, legend says, Mary placed the infant Jesus in Cajetan's arms. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
o.b: A priest of Vicenza who co-founded the Theatines to renew the clergy. He opened hospitals and pawnshops for the poor, and is patron of job-seekers.

2027-08-07.t: Saint Sixtus II, Pope, and Companions, Martyrs

w.a: Christ Healing the Boy Possessed by a Demon, a panel of the Sherborne Almshouse Triptych, Flemish, about 1480–90. The father brings his son to Jesus, and beyond them the blind Bartimaeus is healed. It belongs to the Almshouse of Saint John in Sherborne, England.
w.b: “For truly, I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from hence to yonder place,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible to you.”
w.by: Master of the Sherborne Almshouse Triptych
w.t: Saturday of the eighteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-08.a: The Last Supper by Dieric Bouts, 1464–68, the center of his Altarpiece of the Holy Sacrament, commissioned by a Eucharistic confraternity. Christ blesses the host. It still hangs in St. Peter's Church in Leuven, Belgium, where it was made.
2027-08-08.b: “I am the living bread which came down from heaven; if any one eats of this bread, he will live for ever; and the bread which I shall give for the life of the world is my flesh.”

2027-08-09.a: Edith Stein around 1938–39, the 'passport photo' taken at the Cologne Carmel before she fled to the Netherlands. In 1942 the Nazis arrested her there and she died at Auschwitz.
2027-08-09.b: Edith Stein, a Jewish-born philosopher who became a Catholic and a Carmelite nun. She was murdered at Auschwitz and is a patron of Europe.

2027-08-09.t: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross Stein, Virgin and Martyr

w.a: The Tribute Money by Masaccio, about 1425, in the Brancacci Chapel of Santa Maria del Carmine, Florence. In one fresco Peter is told to catch a fish, finds the coin in its mouth at the lakeside, and hands it to the tax collector.
w.b: “Go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a shekel; take that and give it to them for me and for yourself.”
w.t: Monday of the nineteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-10.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence by Titian, 1548–59, one of the first great night pictures in Western art, lit by torches and the fire beneath the gridiron. It is in the Chiesa dei Gesuiti, Venice.
2027-08-10.b: A deacon of Rome in charge of the Church's goods. Ordered to hand over its treasures, he brought the poor and said, 'Here are the treasures of the Church.' He was martyred on a gridiron.

2027-08-11.a: Saint Clare by Simone Martini, about 1317–20, in the Lower Church of San Francesco, Assisi—the city where she lived and died. It is the classic image of her in the brown habit of her Poor Clares.
2027-08-11.b: A noblewoman of Assisi who ran away at eighteen to follow St. Francis in poverty. She founded the Poor Clares and led them from San Damiano for forty years.

2027-08-12.a: Saint Francis de Sales Giving Saint Jane de Chantal the Rule of the Visitation, by Noël Hallé, 18th century. It hangs in the church of Saint-Louis-en-l'Île, Paris.
2027-08-12.b: A widowed mother of four who, guided by St. Francis de Sales, founded the Order of the Visitation for women who could not bear the rigors of older orders.

o.a: Saint Francis de Sales Giving Saint Jane de Chantal the Rule of the Visitation, by Noël Hallé, 18th century. It hangs in the church of Saint-Louis-en-l'Île, Paris.
o.b: A widowed mother of four who, guided by St. Francis de Sales, founded the Order of the Visitation for women who could not bear the rigors of older orders.
o.t: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal, Religious

2027-08-12.t: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal, Religious

w.a: The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant by Claude Vignon, 1629: the servant who was forgiven a great debt but would not forgive a small one.
w.b: “Then Peter came up and said to him, ‘Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? As many as seven times?’ Jesus said to him, ‘I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven.’”
w.t: Thursday of the nineteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-13.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Hippolytus by Dieric Bouts and Hugo van der Goes, about 1470–75. According to legend, Hippolytus was tied to four horses and torn apart. It is in St. Salvator's Cathedral, Bruges.
2027-08-13.b: A pope and a rival scholar-priest who had broken with him, both sent to the mines of Sardinia. There they were reconciled and died as martyrs.
2027-08-13.by: Hugo van der Goes / Dieric Bouts

o.b: A pope and a rival scholar-priest who had broken with him, both sent to the mines of Sardinia. There they were reconciled and died as martyrs.
o.by: Hugo van der Goes / Dieric Bouts
o.t: Saints Pontian, Pope, and Hippolytus, Priest, Martyrs

2027-08-13.t: Saints Pontian, Pope, and Hippolytus, Priest, Martyrs

w.a: Adam and Eve by Albrecht Dürer, 1507, two panels painted after his second journey to Italy. 'From the beginning it was not so.' It is in the Prado, Madrid.
w.b: “For your hardness of heart Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so.”
w.t: Friday of the nineteenth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-14.a: Father Maximilian Kolbe in 1936, the year he returned from founding a friary near Nagasaki. Five years later in Auschwitz he took the place of a condemned father of a family.
2027-08-14.b: A Polish Franciscan who founded the Knights of the Immaculata. At Auschwitz he offered his life in place of a stranger with a family, and died in the starvation bunker.
2027-08-14.t: Saint Maximilian Mary Kolbe, Priest and Martyr

2027-08-15.a: The Assumption of the Virgin by Titian, 1516–18, the enormous altarpiece that made his name. Nearly seven meters high, it still stands above the high altar of the Frari church in Venice, where it was unveiled to the city's astonishment.
2027-08-15.b: At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken body and soul into the glory of heaven. One of the oldest Marian feasts, it is kept on August 15 throughout the Church.
2027-08-15.t: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-08-16.a: Saint Stephen of Hungary Receiving the Papal Legate by Pieter Jozef Verhaghen, 1770. The pope's envoy brings the crown for Hungary's first king. It is in the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.
2027-08-16.b: The first King of Hungary, crowned with a crown sent by the pope in 1000. He brought the faith to his people, founded dioceses and is revered as the father of the nation.

o.a: Saint Stephen of Hungary Receiving the Papal Legate by Pieter Jozef Verhaghen, 1770. The pope's envoy brings the crown for Hungary's first king. It is in the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.
o.b: The first King of Hungary, crowned with a crown sent by the pope in 1000. He brought the faith to his people, founded dioceses and is revered as the father of the nation.

w.a: Saint Anthony Distributing His Wealth to the Poor by the Master of the Osservanza, about 1430–35. Hearing this very Gospel read in church, the young Anthony gave away everything he owned. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
w.b: “If you would be perfect, go, sell what you possess and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
w.t: Monday of the twentieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-17.a: Christ and the Rich Young Man by Andrey Mironov, a contemporary Russian painter of Gospel scenes who shares his work freely. The young man turns away, and Jesus tells his disciples how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom.
2027-08-17.b: “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
2027-08-17.t: Tuesday of the twentieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-18.a: The Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard by Rembrandt, 1637. At day's end the landowner pays the workers in a dim barn, while those who worked all day complain. It is in the Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.
2027-08-18.b: “Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or do you begrudge my generosity?”
2027-08-18.t: Wednesday of the twentieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-19.a: Saint John Eudes, a 17th-century portrait. The Norman missionary was the first to write a Mass in honor of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary.
2027-08-19.b: A French priest and preacher who founded seminaries and religious congregations, and promoted devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

o.a: Saint John Eudes, a 17th-century portrait. The Norman missionary was the first to write a Mass in honor of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary.
o.b: A French priest and preacher who founded seminaries and religious congregations, and promoted devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

w.a: The Parable of the Royal Wedding by Pieter Aertsen, about 1570. The king's servants bring in guests from the streets to fill the wedding feast.
w.b: “For many are called, but few are chosen.”
w.t: Thursday of the twentieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-20.a: The Vision of Saint Bernard by Filippino Lippi, about 1485. The Virgin appears to Bernard as he writes at a desk among the rocks, with angels at her side. It still hangs in the Badia Fiorentina, Florence.
2027-08-20.b: A French Cistercian abbot whose eloquence moved popes and kings and helped spread his order across Europe. His writings on the love of God and devotion to Mary earned him the name 'the honey-sweet doctor'.
2027-08-20.t: Saint Bernard, Abbot and Doctor of the Church

2027-08-21.a: Pope Pius X, photographed by Ernest Walter Histed. The son of a village postman, he lowered the age of first communion so that children could receive it.
2027-08-21.b: Giuseppe Sarto, pope from 1903 to 1914, whose motto was 'to restore all things in Christ'. He encouraged frequent Communion and let children receive it young.

2027-08-22.a: Christ's Charge to Peter by Raphael, 1515–16, a design for one of the tapestries he made for the Sistine Chapel. Peter kneels with the keys before the risen Christ, as the other apostles watch. The full-size design is in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.
2027-08-22.b: “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.”

2027-08-23.a: Saint Rose of Lima, attributed to José del Pozo, about 1810–20. The first saint of the Americas wears her crown of roses, beneath which she hid a band of spikes. It is in the Lima Art Museum.
2027-08-23.b: The first canonized saint of the Americas, she lived a life of prayer and penance in her family's garden in Lima, serving the poor and sick.

o.a: Saint Rose of Lima, attributed to José del Pozo, about 1810–20. The first saint of the Americas wears her crown of roses, beneath which she hid a band of spikes. It is in the Lima Art Museum.
o.b: The first canonized saint of the Americas, she lived a life of prayer and penance in her family's garden in Lima, serving the poor and sick.

w.a: Woe unto You, Scribes and Pharisees by James Tissot, from his watercolors of the life of Christ, 1886–94. Jesus confronts the scribes and Pharisees in the Temple. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
w.b: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you shut the kingdom of heaven against men.”
w.t: Monday of the twenty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-24.a: Saint Bartholomew, from Michelangelo's Last Judgment, 1536–41, on the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel. He holds the knife and his own flayed skin, and the face on the skin is thought to be Michelangelo's self-portrait.
2027-08-24.b: One of the Twelve, often identified with Nathanael, of whom Jesus said, 'Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile.' Tradition says he preached in the East and was martyred there.

2027-08-25.a: Saint Louis, King of France, with a Page, by El Greco, about 1592–95. The crusader king holds his scepter while a page carries his crown. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-08-25.b: King of France renowned for justice and care for the poor. He built the Sainte-Chapelle and died on crusade near Tunis.

o.a: Saint Louis, King of France, with a Page, by El Greco, about 1592–95. The crusader king holds his scepter while a page carries his crown. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
o.b: King of France renowned for justice and care for the poor. He built the Sainte-Chapelle and died on crusade near Tunis.

o.a: The Last Communion of Saint Joseph Calasanz by Francisco de Goya, 1819, painted for the Piarist church of San Antón in Madrid. Goya had studied at a Piarist school as a boy and refused most of his fee. It is still in San Antón.
o.b: A Spanish priest who opened one of Europe's first free public schools, in Rome,, and founded the Piarists to teach poor children.

w.a: Absalom's Pillar, Valley of Jehoshaphat by David Roberts, 1839. The ancient tombs cut into the rock of the Kidron Valley, just outside the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the Cleveland Museum of Art.
w.b: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within they are full of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness.”
w.t: Wednesday of the twenty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-26.a: The Wise and Foolish Virgins by Wilhelm von Schadow, 1838–42, a leader of the German Nazarene painters. Christ the bridegroom welcomes the wise virgins with their lamps lit, while the foolish ones arrive too late. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.
2027-08-26.b: “Blessed is that servant whom his master when he comes will find so doing.”
2027-08-26.t: Thursday of the twenty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-27.a: Saint Augustine and Saint Monica by Ary Scheffer, painted in the 1850s. Mother and son sit at a window at Ostia, gazing upward, as in Augustine's account of their shared vision of heaven days before her death. This version is in the Musée de la Vie Romantique, Scheffer's own house in Paris.
2027-08-27.b: Mother of St. Augustine, who prayed for his conversion for many years. She died at Ostia shortly after his baptism.

2027-08-28.a: Saint Augustine by Philippe de Champaigne, about 1645–50. The flaming heart in his hand and the beam marked Veritas, truth, sum up his life's search. It is in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
2027-08-28.b: After a restless youth he was converted in Milan, moved by the prayers of his mother, Monica. As bishop of Hippo he wrote the Confessions and The City of God; he is a Doctor of the Church.
2027-08-28.t: Saint Augustine, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-08-29.a: Jesus and the Pharisees by Gustave Doré. The Pharisees press Jesus with questions in a narrow street, trying to catch him out. Doré made hundreds of Bible engravings, reprinted around the world.
2027-08-29.b: “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.’”

2027-08-30.a: Christ in the Synagogue at Nazareth, a drawing from a series on the life of Christ. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-08-30.b: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
2027-08-30.t: Monday of the twenty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-08-31.a: The Healings of Christ, an engraving from a series of Bible scenes, showing the cures at Capernaum. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-08-31.b: “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.”
2027-08-31.t: Tuesday of the twenty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-01.a: Christ Healing the Mother of Simon Peter's Wife by John Bridges, 1839, an English painter. Christ takes the sick woman by the hand as the family watches.
2027-09-01.b: “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose.”
2027-09-01.t: Wednesday of the twenty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-02.a: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes by Raphael, 1515–16, a full-size design for a tapestry for the Sistine Chapel. Peter kneels in the overloaded boat: 'Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.' It is lent by the King to the Victoria and Albert Museum, London.
2027-09-02.b: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.”
2027-09-02.t: Thursday of the twenty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-03.a: Saint Gregory the Great by Francisco de Goya, 1796–99, one of his four Doctors of the Church. The pope writes at his desk in his tiara and robes. It is in the Museo del Romanticismo, Madrid.
2027-09-03.b: A Roman prefect turned monk, then pope. He sent missionaries to England, reformed the liturgy and cared for Rome in famine and plague. He is a Doctor of the Church.
2027-09-03.t: Saint Gregory the Great, Pope and Doctor of the Church

2027-09-04.a: The Disciples Pick Grain on the Sabbath, a panel of the Gotha Altarpiece, about 1540, from the workshop of Heinrich Füllmaurer — 157 painted scenes of the life of Christ in one folding altarpiece. It is in Friedenstein Castle, Gotha.
2027-09-04.b: “The Son of man is lord of the sabbath.”
2027-09-04.by: artist: Heinrich Füllmaurer, photographer: Lutz Ebhardt
2027-09-04.t: Saturday of the twenty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-05.a: Christ Giving His Blessing by Hans Memling, 1478. Christ looks straight out at the viewer and raises his hand in blessing, as if speaking the healing word 'Ephphatha'. It is in the Norton Simon Museum, Pasadena, California.
2027-09-05.b: “Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, ‘Ephphatha,’ that is, ‘Be opened.’”

2027-09-06.a: The Healing of the Man with the Withered Hand, from the Hitda Codex, about 1000–20, painted in Cologne for Abbess Hitda of Meschede. Christ stretches out his hand toward the man across a blue sea of figures. It is in the University and State Library, Darmstadt.
2027-09-06.b: “He looked around on them all, and said to him, ‘Stretch out your hand.’ And he did so, and his hand was restored.”
2027-09-06.t: Monday of the twenty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-07.a: Christ Chooses His Apostles, an engraving from the Emblemata Novi Testamenti, a 17th-century Flemish picture book of the Gospels. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-09-07.b: “In these days he went out into the hills to pray; and all night he continued in prayer to God.”
2027-09-07.t: Tuesday of the twenty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-08.a: The Birth of the Virgin by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1660, painted for Seville Cathedral. The newborn Mary glows in the arms of the midwives as angels crowd in to see her. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-09-08.b: The birthday of Mary, daughter of Joachim and Anne, celebrated nine months after the feast of her Immaculate Conception.
2027-09-08.t: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-09-09.a: Saint Peter Claver, an 18th-century painting in the Church of St. Ignatius, Bogotá. He met every slave ship arriving at Cartagena, and called himself 'the slave of the slaves forever.'
2027-09-09.b: A Spanish Jesuit in Cartagena, Colombia, who met every slave ship for forty years, nursing and baptizing the enslaved. He called himself 'the slave of the slaves forever.'
