2027-09-10.a: The Parable of the Blind by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1568. Six blind men, holding on to each other, stumble one after another toward the ditch. It is in the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.
2027-09-10.b: “Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?”
2027-09-10.t: Friday of the twenty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-11.a: The House on the Rock, a 17th-century Dutch engraving from a series of 24 scenes from the New Testament. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-09-11.b: “He is like a man building a house, who dug deep, and laid the foundation upon rock; and when a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it had been well built.”
2027-09-11.t: Saturday of the twenty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-12.a: The Delivery of the Keys by Pietro Perugino, 1481–82, on the wall of the Sistine Chapel. Christ gives the keys of the kingdom to the kneeling Peter, in a vast piazza before an ideal temple.
2027-09-12.b: “He asked them, ‘But who do you say that I am?’ Peter answered him, ‘You are the Christ.’”

2027-09-13.a: Saint John Chrysostom, a mosaic of the late 800s in the north tympanum of Hagia Sophia, Istanbul, where he was archbishop. His name, 'golden-mouthed', is spelled out in gold beside him.
2027-09-13.b: Archbishop of Constantinople whose preaching earned him the name 'Golden Mouth'. He died in exile for denouncing corruption, and is a Doctor of the Church.
2027-09-13.t: Saint John Chrysostom, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-09-14.a: Heraclius Carrying the Cross, from the Frankfurt altarpiece of the Exaltation of the True Cross by Adam Elsheimer, about 1603–05. Painted on copper, it is barely larger than a book. The emperor brings the Cross back to Jerusalem barefoot, having laid aside his crown. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.
2027-09-14.b: A feast of the cross on which Christ died, recalling the finding of the True Cross in Jerusalem and the dedication of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in 335. The instrument of death becomes the sign of victory.
2027-09-14.t: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross

2027-09-15.a: Mater Dolorosa with Clasped Hands by Titian, 1554, painted for the Emperor Charles V, who kept it with him when he retired to the monastery of Yuste. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-09-15.b: Mary's sorrows, from Simeon's prophecy to the burial of her Son. 'A sword will pierce your own soul too.'

2027-09-16.a: Saint Cyprian by the Master of Messkirch, about 1535–40, from the side altars of St. Martin's Church in Messkirch. It is in the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.
2027-09-16.b: Pope Cornelius and Bishop Cyprian of Carthage stood together for mercy toward Christians who had lapsed under persecution. Both died for the faith.
2027-09-16.t: Saints Cornelius, Pope, and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs

2027-09-17.a: Hildegard receiving a vision, from the Rupertsberg manuscript of her Scivias, made under her supervision around 1180. Flames of light descend on her head as she writes on a wax tablet and the monk Volmar takes it down. The original was lost in 1945; a hand-painted copy survives.
2027-09-17.b: A Benedictine abbess, visionary, composer and writer on medicine and nature. Declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.

o.a: Hildegard receiving a vision, from the Rupertsberg manuscript of her Scivias, made under her supervision around 1180. Flames of light descend on her head as she writes on a wax tablet and the monk Volmar takes it down. The original was lost in 1945; a hand-painted copy survives.
o.b: A Benedictine abbess, visionary, composer and writer on medicine and nature. Declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
o.t: Saint Hildegard of Bingen, Abbess and Doctor of the Church

o.a: Cardinal Robert Bellarmine, painted around 1622, the year after his death. It hangs in the Museum Plantin-Moretus in Antwerp, once the most important printing house in Europe.
o.b: A Jesuit cardinal and theologian who wrote catechisms and great works of controversy with humility and charity. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Robert Bellarmine, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-09-17.t: Saint Hildegard of Bingen, Abbess and Doctor of the Church

w.a: Mary Magdalene by Carlo Crivelli, about 1480. She holds the jar of ointment, dressed in rich brocade. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
w.b: “Soon afterward he went on through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of the kingdom of God. And the twelve were with him.”
w.t: Friday of the twenty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-18.a: The Sower by Jean-François Millet, 1850. A peasant strides down a dark hillside flinging seed, while crows follow. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and later inspired Van Gogh.
2027-09-18.b: “As for that in the good soil, they are those who, hearing the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bring forth fruit with patience.”
2027-09-18.t: Saturday of the twenty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-19.a: Head of Christ by Correggio, about 1525–30, painted as if on Veronica's veil. Christ looks out at the viewer with quiet tenderness. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.
2027-09-19.b: “If any one would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”

2027-09-20.a: Andrew Kim Taegon, from an oil portrait by the Korean painter Louis Chang, about 1920. Kim was the first Korean-born priest; he was beheaded near Seoul in 1846 at twenty-five.
2027-09-20.b: Andrew Kim was the first Korean-born priest, beheaded at twenty-five. With the lay catechist Paul Chong and 101 companions, he is honored among the martyrs of the Church in Korea.
2027-09-20.t: Saints Andrew Kim Tae-gŏn, Priest, Paul Chŏng Ha-sang and Companions, Martyrs

2027-09-21.a: The Calling of Saint Matthew by Caravaggio, 1599–1600, his first great public commission. A beam of light follows Christ's pointing hand across a tavern table to the tax collector. It still hangs in the Contarelli Chapel of San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome.
2027-09-21.b: A tax collector at Capernaum who left his booth when Jesus said, 'Follow me.' Tradition names him as the author of the first Gospel, and as a martyr.

2027-09-22.a: Christ Sends Out the Twelve Apostles, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-09-22.b: “He sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal.”
2027-09-22.t: Wednesday of the twenty-fifth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-23.a: Padre Pio around 1947. He bore the stigmata for fifty years and drew crowds to the friary of San Giovanni Rotondo, where he heard confessions for up to sixteen hours a day.
2027-09-23.b: Padre Pio, a Capuchin friar of San Giovanni Rotondo who bore the stigmata for fifty years. Crowds came to his confessional and his Mass.

2027-09-24.a: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter by Guido Reni, about 1624–26. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-09-24.b: “He said to them, ‘But who do you say that I am?’ And Peter answered, ‘The Christ of God.’”
2027-09-24.t: Friday of the twenty-fifth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-25.a: Christ Carrying the Cross by El Greco, about 1577–87. Christ embraces the cross, his eyes raised to heaven. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-09-25.b: “Let these words sink into your ears; for the Son of man is to be delivered into the hands of men.”
2027-09-25.t: Saturday of the twenty-fifth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-26.a: The Blessing Christ by Giovanni Bellini, about 1465–70. The risen Christ, his wounds visible, raises his hand in blessing against a dawn landscape. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-09-26.b: “For truly, I say to you, whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you bear the name of Christ, will by no means lose his reward.”

2027-09-27.a: Vincent de Paul by Simon François de Tours, the portrait painted in his lifetime and the best-known likeness of him. His kindly, weathered face became the image of charity in France.
2027-09-27.b: A French peasant's son who became a priest and gave his life to the poor, the sick and galley slaves. With St. Louise de Marillac he founded the Daughters of Charity.

2027-09-28.a: The Saint Wenceslas Monument by Josef Václav Myslbek, completed in 1912, at the top of Wenceslas Square in Prague. It has been the city's great rallying point, where crowds gathered in 1918, 1968 and 1989.
2027-09-28.b: Duke of Bohemia, the 'Good King Wenceslas' of the carol, known for his piety and charity. He was murdered by his brother and is patron of the Czech lands.

o.a: The Saint Wenceslas Monument by Josef Václav Myslbek, completed in 1912, at the top of Wenceslas Square in Prague. It has been the city's great rallying point, where crowds gathered in 1918, 1968 and 1989.
o.b: Duke of Bohemia, the 'Good King Wenceslas' of the carol, known for his piety and charity. He was murdered by his brother and is patron of the Czech lands.

o.a: Lorenzo Ruiz in stained glass at Cubao Cathedral, Quezon City. A Manila calligrapher and father of three, he fled to Japan and was martyred at Nagasaki in 1637, the first Filipino saint.
o.b: A Filipino husband and father who joined Dominican missionaries to Japan and was martyred at Nagasaki with fifteen companions. He is the first Filipino saint.
o.t: Saint Lawrence Ruiz and Companions, Martyrs

w.a: Christ and His Disciples by the Flemish Master of the Prodigal Son, 1500s. Jesus walks with his disciples through the countryside.
w.b: “When the days drew near for him to be received up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.”
w.t: Tuesday of the twenty-sixth week of Ordinary Time

2027-09-29.a: The Fall of the Rebel Angels by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1562. Michael, in gleaming armor, drives the fallen angels from heaven as they turn into fantastic monsters. It is in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts, Brussels.
2027-09-29.b: The three archangels named in Scripture: Michael, who casts down Satan; Gabriel, who brought the news to Mary; and Raphael, who guided Tobias and healed his father.
2027-09-29.t: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels

2027-09-30.a: Saint Jerome Writing by Caravaggio, 1607–08, painted in Malta for the knight Ippolito Malaspina, whose coat of arms is in the corner. Stolen in 1984 and recovered in 1988, it hangs in St. John's Co-Cathedral, Valletta.
2027-09-30.b: A brilliant and fiery scholar who lived as a monk in Bethlehem and translated the Bible into Latin. His Vulgate was the Church's Bible for over a thousand years; he is patron of translators.
2027-09-30.t: Saint Jerome, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-10-01.a: Thérèse in the cloister of the Lisieux Carmel, photographed by her sister Céline in 1896, a year before she died. She holds a parchment with words of St. Teresa of Ávila: 'I would give a thousand lives to save one soul.'
2027-10-01.b: A Carmelite nun of Lisieux who died at twenty-four. Her 'little way' of trust and love, told in Story of a Soul, made her a Doctor of the Church.
2027-10-01.t: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus, Virgin and Doctor of the Church

2027-10-02.a: The Guardian Angel by Domenichino, 1615. The angel shields a child with one hand and drives off the devil with the other. It is in the Capodimonte Museum, Naples.
2027-10-02.b: The Church gives thanks for the angels God sends to guard and guide each person: 'He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.'

2027-10-03.a: Christ Blessing the Children by Lucas Cranach the Elder, painted after 1537, one of several versions from his workshop. Mothers crowd around Jesus with their babies. It is in the National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen.
2027-10-03.b: “Let the children come to me, do not hinder them; for to such belongs the kingdom of God.”

2027-10-04.a: Saint Francis in the Desert by Giovanni Bellini, about 1480. Francis steps out of his cave into a flood of light, arms open, perhaps at the moment of the stigmata. It is often called the greatest Italian Renaissance painting in America. It is in the Frick Collection, New York.
2027-10-04.b: The son of a rich merchant who gave up everything to live in poverty and joy, preaching peace and caring for lepers. He founded the Franciscans, received the stigmata, and is patron of animals and the environment.

2027-10-05.a: Sister Faustina in Płock, 1931, the year Jesus first appeared to her there as the Divine Mercy and asked her to have his image painted.
2027-10-05.b: A Polish nun whose diary of visions spread devotion to the Divine Mercy and the image inscribed 'Jesus, I trust in you.'

o.a: Sister Faustina in Płock, 1931, the year Jesus first appeared to her there as the Divine Mercy and asked her to have his image painted.
o.b: A Polish nun whose diary of visions spread devotion to the Divine Mercy and the image inscribed 'Jesus, I trust in you.'

o.a: Francis Xavier Seelos around 1855. The Bavarian Redemptorist preached across America and died in New Orleans in 1867, nursing victims of yellow fever.
o.b: A Bavarian Redemptorist who served German immigrants across the United States. He died in New Orleans after caring for victims of yellow fever.

w.a: Kitchen Scene with Christ in the House of Martha and Mary by Diego Velázquez, 1618, painted when he was nineteen. A sulking servant pounds garlic in the kitchen, while through a hatch Mary sits at Christ's feet. It is in the National Gallery, London.
w.b: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things; one thing is needful. Mary has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her.”
w.t: Tuesday of the twenty-seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-06.a: Saint Bruno in Prayer by Domingos Sequeira, 1799–1800, painted for the Carthusian monastery of Laveiras near Lisbon. Sequeira was Portugal's leading painter of his day. It is in the National Museum of Ancient Art, Lisbon.
2027-10-06.b: A German scholar who left a brilliant career at Reims to seek God in silence. In the mountains near Grenoble he founded the Carthusians, monks who live as hermits in community.

o.a: Saint Bruno in Prayer by Domingos Sequeira, 1799–1800, painted for the Carthusian monastery of Laveiras near Lisbon. Sequeira was Portugal's leading painter of his day. It is in the National Museum of Ancient Art, Lisbon.
o.b: A German scholar who left a brilliant career at Reims to seek God in silence. In the mountains near Grenoble he founded the Carthusians, monks who live as hermits in community.

o.a: Marie-Rose Durocher, a copy of the portrait by Théophile Hamel. She founded the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus and Mary in Quebec to teach poor children.
o.b: A Canadian who founded the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus and Mary to educate children in Quebec.

w.a: The Lord's Prayer by James Tissot, from his watercolors of the life of Christ, 1886–94. Jesus sits among his disciples, teaching them to pray. It is in the Brooklyn Museum, New York.
w.b: “Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples.”
w.t: Wednesday of the twenty-seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-07.a: The Madonna of the Rosary by Caravaggio, about 1605–07. Dominic hands out rosaries to the poor. Rubens and other Antwerp artists bought it for the Dominican church there; it is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-10-07.b: Instituted after the victory at Lepanto in 1571, attributed to the praying of the Rosary. The Rosary is a meditation on the life of Christ with Mary.

2027-10-08.a: Christ Heals a Possessed Man before the Pharisees and Scribes, a 16th-century Netherlandish engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-10-08.b: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters.”
2027-10-08.t: Friday of the twenty-seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-09.a: Cardinal Newman by Sir John Everett Millais, 1881, painted two years after Newman was made a cardinal at seventy-eight. It belongs to the National Portrait Gallery, London.
2027-10-09.b: An Anglican leader of the Oxford Movement who became a Catholic and later a cardinal. A writer of rare clarity, he was canonized in 2019.

o.a: The Altarpiece of Saint Denis by Henri Bellechose, 1416, painted for the Charterhouse of Champmol in Dijon. Christ gives Denis his last communion in prison, and beside it he and his companions are beheaded. It is in the Louvre.
o.b: The first Bishop of Paris, beheaded on the hill now called Montmartre, 'the martyrs' mount', with the priest Rusticus and the deacon Eleutherius. Legend says he walked away carrying his head.
o.t: Saint Denis, Bishop, and Companions, Martyrs

o.a: Saint John Leonardi with the Virgin and Child, an altar painting showing the founder among the young people he taught. A pharmacist's assistant turned priest, he helped found the Vatican's college for training missionaries.
o.b: A pharmacist turned priest in Lucca, he founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God and helped establish what became the Church's college for the missions.

o.a: Cardinal Newman by Sir John Everett Millais, 1881, painted two years after Newman was made a cardinal at seventy-eight. It belongs to the National Portrait Gallery, London.
o.b: An Anglican leader of the Oxford Movement who became a Catholic and later a cardinal. A writer of rare clarity, he was canonized in 2019.
o.t: Saint John Henry Newman, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-10-09.t: Saint John Henry Newman, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: The Lucca Madonna by Jan van Eyck, about 1437. Mary sits enthroned in a small room and nurses the Christ Child. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.
w.b: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!”
w.t: Saturday of the twenty-seventh week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-10.a: Christ and the Rich Young Ruler by Heinrich Hofmann, 1889, one of the best-loved religious paintings of its time. Jesus points the young man to the poor at his side. It hangs in Riverside Church, New York.
2027-10-10.b: “You lack one thing; go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

2027-10-11.a: Pope John XXIII, from a portrait of 1958–63. Expected to be a short 'caretaker' pope at seventy-six, he surprised the world by calling the Second Vatican Council.
2027-10-11.b: Angelo Roncalli, the warm-hearted 'Good Pope John', who opened the Second Vatican Council in 1962 to renew the Church.

o.a: Pope John XXIII, from a portrait of 1958–63. Expected to be a short 'caretaker' pope at seventy-six, he surprised the world by calling the Second Vatican Council.
o.b: Angelo Roncalli, the warm-hearted 'Good Pope John', who opened the Second Vatican Council in 1962 to renew the Church.

w.a: Seascape with Jonah and the Whale by Gaspard Dughet, about 1653–54. Lightning splits the sky over a storm-tossed sea as Jonah is thrown to the great fish. It is in the Royal Collection.
w.b: “The men of Nineveh will arise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.”
w.t: Monday of the twenty-eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-12.a: The Dinner at the House of the Pharisee by Maria Felice Tibaldi Subleyras, about 1737, a small copy in miniature of her husband Pierre Subleyras's great canvas. It is in the Galleria Sabauda, Turin.
2027-10-12.b: “But give for alms those things which are within; and behold, everything is clean for you.”
2027-10-12.t: Tuesday of the twenty-eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-13.a: Christ Speaks to the Scribes and Pharisees, an engraving in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-10-13.b: “But woe to you Pharisees! for you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and neglect justice and the love of God; these you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.”
2027-10-13.t: Wednesday of the twenty-eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-14.a: Pope Callistus I, a portrait from the great series of papal portraits on the walls of the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls, Rome, begun in the 5th century. It survived the fire that destroyed the basilica in 1823.
2027-10-14.b: Once a slave, he became a deacon in charge of the Christian cemetery on the Appian Way that bears his name, then pope. He was martyred in Rome.

o.a: Pope Callistus I, a portrait from the great series of papal portraits on the walls of the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls, Rome, begun in the 5th century. It survived the fire that destroyed the basilica in 1823.
o.b: Once a slave, he became a deacon in charge of the Christian cemetery on the Appian Way that bears his name, then pope. He was martyred in Rome.
o.t: Saint Callistus I, Pope and Martyr

2027-10-14.t: Saint Callistus I, Pope and Martyr

w.a: The Tomb of Absalom by Vasily Polenov, 1882, painted in the Kidron Valley below the walls of Jerusalem, among the old tombs of kings and prophets. It is in the Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts.
w.b: “Woe to you lawyers! for you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering.”
w.t: Thursday of the twenty-eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-15.a: The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1647–52. An angel holds a golden arrow, just as Teresa described in her autobiography. It is the centerpiece of the Cornaro Chapel in Santa Maria della Vittoria, Rome.
2027-10-15.b: A Spanish Carmelite nun, mystic and reformer who founded seventeen convents and wrote The Interior Castle. Bold and humorous, she was the first woman named a Doctor of the Church.
2027-10-15.t: Saint Teresa of Jesus, Virgin and Doctor of the Church

2027-10-16.a: The Vision of the Sacred Heart, a 19th-century canvas in the sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Acero in the Apennines. In the convent chapel at Paray-le-Monial, Christ shows Margaret Mary his heart, 'which has so loved mankind.'
2027-10-16.b: A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial whose visions of Christ spread devotion to his Sacred Heart throughout the Church.

o.a: Saint Hedwig with Duke Ludwig of Legnica and Duchess Agnes, from the Hedwig Codex, 1353. She holds a statue of the Virgin, a rosary and the shoes she carried rather than wore, to walk barefoot. It is in the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.
o.b: A Bavarian-born duchess of Silesia who used her position to found hospitals and monasteries. After her husband's death she lived among the nuns of Trzebnica, serving the poor.
o.by: Court workshop of Duke Ludwig I of Liegnitz and Brieg

o.a: The Vision of the Sacred Heart, a 19th-century canvas in the sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Acero in the Apennines. In the convent chapel at Paray-le-Monial, Christ shows Margaret Mary his heart, 'which has so loved mankind.'
o.b: A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial whose visions of Christ spread devotion to his Sacred Heart throughout the Church.

w.a: Saint Stephen Preaching and Saint Stephen Addressing the Council by Fra Angelico, 1448–50, in the Niccoline Chapel of the Vatican. Stephen speaks, full of the Holy Spirit, first to the people and then to the council.
w.b: “For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say.”
w.t: Saturday of the twenty-eighth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-17.a: Christ and the Sons of Zebedee by Ambrosius Francken the Elder, 1610, a wing of the altarpiece of St. James's Church in Antwerp. Their mother asks for places of honor for her sons, James and John.
2027-10-17.b: “For the Son of man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

2027-10-18.a: Saint Luke Drawing the Virgin by Rogier van der Weyden, about 1435–40, perhaps with Rogier's own face as Luke. It was probably made for the painters' guild of Brussels, whose patron Luke was. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
2027-10-18.b: A Greek physician and companion of St. Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles. Tradition says he painted the first icon of the Virgin; he is patron of doctors and artists.

2027-10-19.a: The Martyrdom of Jean de Brébeuf and Gabriel Lalemant, in the Cathedral-Basilica of Mary, Queen of the World, Montreal. Brébeuf preached to his Iroquois captors until they silenced him.
2027-10-19.b: French Jesuit missionaries and lay companions who lived among the Huron and Iroquois peoples and were martyred there. They are the patron saints of North America.
2027-10-19.t: Saints John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues, Priests, and Companions, Martyrs

2027-10-20.a: Saint Paul of the Cross, engraved by G. B. Leonetti after a painting by A. Tofanelli. The founder of the Passionists preached the Passion of Christ across Italy. It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
2027-10-20.b: An Italian mystic and preacher who founded the Passionists, devoted to preaching the Passion of Christ.

o.a: Saint Paul of the Cross, engraved by G. B. Leonetti after a painting by A. Tofanelli. The founder of the Passionists preached the Passion of Christ across Italy. It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
o.b: An Italian mystic and preacher who founded the Passionists, devoted to preaching the Passion of Christ.
o.t: Saint Paul of the Cross, Priest

2027-10-20.t: Saint Paul of the Cross, Priest

w.a: The Servant Waiting at Night for His Master, an etching by Jan Luyken, 1712. A light burns as the servant stands ready by the door. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
w.b: “You also must be ready; for the Son of man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
w.t: Wednesday of the twenty-ninth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-21.a: Pentecost by Jean Restout, 1732. Tongues of fire descend on the apostles gathered around Mary. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-10-21.b: “I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how I am constrained until it is accomplished!”
2027-10-21.t: Thursday of the twenty-ninth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-22.a: Pope John Paul II in October 1980, two years into his pontificate. Elected in 1978 as the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, he visited 129 countries and was canonized nine years after his death.
2027-10-22.b: Karol Wojtyła of Kraków, pope from 1978 to 2005. He travelled the world, helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe, and called young people to 'Be not afraid.'

o.a: Pope John Paul II in October 1980, two years into his pontificate. Elected in 1978 as the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, he visited 129 countries and was canonized nine years after his death.
o.b: Karol Wojtyła of Kraków, pope from 1978 to 2005. He travelled the world, helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe, and called young people to 'Be not afraid.'

w.a: Wheat Fields by Jacob van Ruisdael, about 1670. Great clouds build over the ripening Dutch fields. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
w.b: “You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of earth and sky; but why do you not know how to interpret the present time?”
w.t: Friday of the twenty-ninth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-23.a: The Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints by Carlo Crivelli, 1488, painted for a Franciscan church in the Marche. John of Capistrano, canonized centuries later, already appears among the Franciscan saints around the throne. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-10-23.b: An Italian lawyer and governor who became a Franciscan and a tireless preacher across Europe. At seventy he helped lead the defense of Belgrade against the Ottoman army.

o.a: The Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints by Carlo Crivelli, 1488, painted for a Franciscan church in the Marche. John of Capistrano, canonized centuries later, already appears among the Franciscan saints around the throne. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
o.b: An Italian lawyer and governor who became a Franciscan and a tireless preacher across Europe. At seventy he helped lead the defense of Belgrade against the Ottoman army.

w.a: September: the Parable of the Barren Fig Tree by Abel Grimmer, from a series of the months. The owner comes looking for fruit and finds none, and the vinedresser begs for one more year.
w.b: “Let it alone, sir, this year also, till I dig about it and put on manure.”
w.t: Saturday of the twenty-ninth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-24.a: Christ Healing the Blind by El Greco, about 1570, painted in Venice before he settled in Spain. Christ touches the blind man's eyes in a deep Italian piazza. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
2027-10-24.b: “Jesus said to him, ‘What do you want me to do for you?’ And the blind man said to him, ‘Master, let me receive my sight.’”

2027-10-25.a: Christ Lays His Hand on the Bent Woman, a 17th-century Dutch engraving. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-10-25.b: “When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, ‘Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.’ And he laid his hands upon her, and immediately she was made straight, and she praised God.”
2027-10-25.t: Monday of the thirtieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-26.a: Woman Baking Bread by Jean-François Millet, 1854. A peasant woman slides the loaves into the oven — the yeast she mixed into the flour has done its work. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, the Netherlands.
2027-10-26.b: “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God? It is like leaven which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.”
2027-10-26.t: Tuesday of the thirtieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-27.a: The Broad and the Narrow Way, a German devotional print designed by Charlotte Reihlen in 1866. The broad road leads through theaters and taverns to the fire; the narrow way climbs past churches and works of mercy to the heavenly city.
2027-10-27.b: “Strive to enter by the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.”
2027-10-27.by: Charlotte Reihlen (Idee); Paul Beckmann (Ausführung); Photo: Andreas Praefcke
2027-10-27.t: Wednesday of the thirtieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-28.a: The Martyrdom of Saints Simon and Jude by Stefan Lochner, about 1435, one of his panels of the deaths of the apostles. Tradition says the two preached together in Persia and were killed there. It is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt.
2027-10-28.b: Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddeus, apostles who, tradition says, preached together in Persia and were martyred there. Jude is invoked as patron of hopeless causes.

2027-10-29.a: Christ Heals a Man with Dropsy at the House of a Pharisee, an 18th-century engraving. It is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
2027-10-29.b: “Which of you, having an ass or an ox that has fallen into a well, will not immediately pull him out on a sabbath day?”
2027-10-29.t: Friday of the thirtieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-30.a: The Peasant Wedding by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, about 1567. Guests crowd a barn for a wedding feast; the bride sits under a paper crown. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-10-30.b: “But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when your host comes he may say to you, ‘Friend, go up higher’; then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at table with you.”
2027-10-30.t: Saturday of the thirtieth week of Ordinary Time

2027-10-31.a: Salvator Mundi by Antonello da Messina, 1465, his earliest dated painting. Christ raises his hand in blessing and rests the other on a ledge; a first, discarded position of the hand is still visible. It is in the National Gallery, London.
2027-10-31.b: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. The second is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

2027-11-01.a: The Adoration of the Trinity, known as the Landauer Altarpiece, by Albrecht Dürer, 1511. The whole Church of heaven and earth—popes, emperors, martyrs and ordinary people—gathers around the Trinity; Dürer painted himself in the corner. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
2027-11-01.b: A feast for every saint in heaven, known and unknown: the 'great multitude which no one could count, from every nation.' It celebrates the holiness of ordinary men and women as much as the famous.

2027-11-02.a: The Day of the Dead by William-Adolphe Bouguereau, 1859. Two women in mourning pray at a grave, the younger leaning on the older in her grief. It is in the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Bordeaux.
2027-11-02.b: All Souls' Day. The Church prays for all who have died, that they may be purified and come to rest in the peace of God.
2027-11-02.t: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed (All Souls’ Day)

2027-11-03.a: A 17th-century portrait of Martin de Porres in the monastery of Santa Rosa de las Monjas in Lima, one of the earliest images of him. He carries a broom, the sign of his humble work.
2027-11-03.b: The son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed Black woman in Lima, he became a Dominican brother known for his care of the sick and the poor. He is patron of social justice.

o.a: A 17th-century portrait of Martin de Porres in the monastery of Santa Rosa de las Monjas in Lima, one of the earliest images of him. He carries a broom, the sign of his humble work.
o.b: The son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed Black woman in Lima, he became a Dominican brother known for his care of the sick and the poor. He is patron of social justice.

w.a: The Tower of Babel by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1563: a tower begun and never finished. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
w.b: “Whoever does not bear his own cross and come after me, cannot be my disciple.”
w.t: Wednesday of the thirty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-04.a: The Fast of Saint Charles Borromeo by Daniele Crespi, about 1628. The cardinal eats only bread and water as he reads, tears on his face. It is in the church of Santa Maria della Passione, Milan.
2027-11-04.b: A nephew of Pope Pius IV, made a cardinal at twenty-two, he became the model reforming bishop of Milan after the Council of Trent. During the plague of 1576 he stayed to feed and nurse the sick.

2027-11-05.a: The Parable of the Unjust Steward, after Marinus van Reymerswaele, 16th century, the Flemish painter of tax collectors and moneylenders. The steward rewrites the debtors' bills at his desk.
2027-11-05.b: “The master commended the dishonest steward for his prudence; for the sons of this world are wiser in their own generation than the sons of light.”
2027-11-05.t: Friday of the thirty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-06.a: The Moneylender and his Wife by Quentin Matsys, 1514. As he weighs gold, his wife turns from her prayer book to watch the coins — God or mammon. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
2027-11-06.b: “He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and he who is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.”
2027-11-06.t: Saturday of the thirty-first week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-07.a: The Widow's Mite by Gustave Doré, from his illustrated Bible of 1866. A poor widow drops her two small coins into the Temple treasury as Jesus watches from the steps.
2027-11-07.b: “Truly, I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are contributing to the treasury. For they all contributed out of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, her whole living.”

2027-11-08.a: The Return of the Prodigal Son by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1667–70 — forgiveness without limit. The father embraces his ragged son while servants bring a robe and a ring and lead in the fatted calf. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-11-08.t: Monday of the thirty-second week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-09.a: The façade of St. John Lateran, Rome, by Alessandro Galilei, 1735, crowned by giant statues of Christ and the saints. The inscription calls it the mother and head of all the churches of the city and the world.
2027-11-09.b: The Lateran is the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome, dedicated in 324, and called 'the mother and head of all churches of the city and the world.'
2027-11-09.t: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica

2027-11-10.a: The Meeting of Leo the Great and Attila by Raphael and his workshop, 1514, in the Vatican's Stanza di Eliodoro. Peter and Paul appear in the sky with swords as Attila turns back from Rome. Leo has the face of Raphael's patron, Pope Leo X.
2027-11-10.b: Pope whose letter, the Tome, guided the Council of Chalcedon on the two natures of Christ. He met Attila the Hun and persuaded him to turn back from Rome.
2027-11-10.t: Saint Leo the Great, Pope and Doctor of the Church

2027-11-11.a: Saint Martin and the Beggar by El Greco, 1597–99, painted for the Chapel of San José in Toledo. Martin, in gold-damascened armor on a white horse, slices his cloak for the beggar. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-11-11.b: A Roman soldier who cut his cloak in half to give to a freezing beggar, and that night saw Christ wearing it. He became a monk and Bishop of Tours, one of the most beloved saints of Europe.

2027-11-12.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Josaphat Kuntsevych by Józef Simmler, about 1861. The archbishop was killed by a mob at Vitebsk in 1623. It is in the National Museum in Warsaw.
2027-11-12.b: A Ukrainian Greek Catholic archbishop of Polotsk who worked for unity between Eastern Christians and Rome, and was martyred for it.

2027-11-13.a: Mother Cabrini around 1900. She crossed the Atlantic more than twenty times and founded sixty-seven schools, orphanages and hospitals; she was the first U.S. citizen to be canonized.
2027-11-13.b: An Italian missionary who founded schools, orphanages and hospitals for immigrants in the Americas. The first U.S. citizen to be canonized, she is patron of immigrants.

2027-11-14.a: The Last Judgment by Hans Memling, about 1467–71. The archangel Michael weighs souls as the dead rise. It was captured by a pirate ship on its way to Florence and has been in Gdańsk, Poland, ever since.
2027-11-14.b: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.”

2027-11-15.a: The Sermon of Saint Albertus Magnus, a German panel by Friedrich Walther, about 1430. The great Dominican scholar preaches to a gathered crowd. It is in The Cloisters, the medieval branch of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.
2027-11-15.b: A German Dominican and bishop who taught St. Thomas Aquinas and wrote on everything from theology to botany. A Doctor of the Church and patron of scientists.

o.a: The Sermon of Saint Albertus Magnus, a German panel by Friedrich Walther, about 1430. The great Dominican scholar preaches to a gathered crowd. It is in The Cloisters, the medieval branch of the Metropolitan Museum, New York.
o.b: A German Dominican and bishop who taught St. Thomas Aquinas and wrote on everything from theology to botany. A Doctor of the Church and patron of scientists.
o.t: Saint Albert the Great, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-11-15.t: Saint Albert the Great, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

w.a: Christ Healing the Blind of Jericho by Nicolas Poussin, 1650. On the road outside the city, Christ touches the eyes of one blind man while the other gropes his way forward. It is in the Louvre, Paris.
w.b: “Receive your sight; your faith has made you well.”
w.t: Monday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-16.a: Queen Saint Margaret of Scotland by Nicolas de Largillière, 1692, one of the leading portrait painters of Louis XIV's France. It hangs at Sizergh Castle in Cumbria, a National Trust house.
2027-11-16.b: An English princess who became Queen of Scotland. She reformed the Church there, founded abbeys and served the poor at her own table.

o.a: Queen Saint Margaret of Scotland by Nicolas de Largillière, 1692, one of the leading portrait painters of Louis XIV's France. It hangs at Sizergh Castle in Cumbria, a National Trust house.
o.b: An English princess who became Queen of Scotland. She reformed the Church there, founded abbeys and served the poor at her own table.

o.a: Saint Gertrude by Miguel Cabrera, 1763, the leading painter of colonial Mexico. Gertrude was hugely popular in New Spain; the Christ Child appears in her heart. It is in the Dallas Museum of Art.
o.b: A Benedictine nun of Helfta whose visions and writings helped spread devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

w.a: Zacchaeus by the Danish painter Niels Larsen Stevns, 1913. Jesus meets the tax collector who climbed a tree to see him.
w.b: “Zacchaeus, make haste and come down; for I must stay at your house today.”
w.t: Tuesday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-17.a: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary by Simone Martini, about 1317–20, among the saints he painted in the Lower Church of San Francesco, Assisi. She died less than a century before, and the Franciscans already counted her as one of their own.
2027-11-17.b: A Hungarian princess and widow who gave her wealth to the poor and built a hospital at Marburg. She died at twenty-four and is patron of Franciscan tertiaries and charities.

2027-11-18.a: St. Peter's, Rome, by Viviano Codazzi, about 1630. Michelangelo's dome had been finished only a few decades earlier. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-11-18.b: A feast of the two great Roman basilicas raised over the tombs of the apostles: St. Peter's on the Vatican Hill and St. Paul's Outside the Walls.

o.a: St. Peter's, Rome, by Viviano Codazzi, about 1630. Michelangelo's dome had been finished only a few decades earlier. It is in the Museo del Prado.
o.b: A feast of the two great Roman basilicas raised over the tombs of the apostles: St. Peter's on the Vatican Hill and St. Paul's Outside the Walls.
o.t: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul, Apostles

o.a: Rose Philippine Duchesne, who founded the first house of the Society of the Sacred Heart in America in 1818. At seventy-one she went to live among the Potawatomi, who called her 'woman who prays always.'
o.b: A French Religious of the Sacred Heart who brought her order to Missouri, opening schools on the frontier. The Potawatomi called her 'Woman Who Prays Always.'

2027-11-18.t: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul, Apostles

w.a: Flevit super illam ('He Wept over It') by Enrique Simonet, 1892. From the Mount of Olives, Christ weeps as he looks across at the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem. It is in the Museo del Prado collection, on loan to the Museum of Málaga.
w.b: “Would that even today you knew the things that make for peace! But now they are hid from your eyes.”
w.t: Thursday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-19.a: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple, a Dutch print after a design by Jacob Jordaens, made between 1652 and 1702. Christ raises a whip of cords as the traders flee and the cattle stampede. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-11-19.b: “It is written, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.”
2027-11-19.t: Friday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-20.a: Christ Teaching in the Temple by Christian Wilhelm Ernst Dietrich, 18th century, a German painter who worked in the manner of Rembrandt.
2027-11-20.b: “For they cannot die any more, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.”
2027-11-20.t: Saturday of the thirty-third week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-21.a: Christ Pantocrator, 'ruler of all', by Angelos Akotantos, the leading Cretan icon painter of the early 1400s. Christ blesses with one hand and holds the Gospel in the other.
2027-11-21.b: The last Sunday of the Church's year proclaims Christ as King of all creation, whose kingdom is 'of truth and life, of holiness and grace, of justice, love and peace.'
2027-11-21.t: Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe

2027-11-22.a: The Ecstasy of Saint Cecilia by Raphael, about 1514–16. Cecilia lets her organ slip as she hears the music of angels; broken instruments lie at her feet. It is in the Pinacoteca Nazionale, Bologna.
2027-11-22.b: A Roman martyr who, tradition says, sang to God in her heart on her wedding day. She is patron of musicians and church music.

2027-11-23.a: Father Miguel Pro on the day of his arrest in 1927, in the civilian clothes he wore to minister in secret. The government photographed his execution to deter others; instead the pictures made him a hero.
2027-11-23.b: A Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during the persecution of the Church. Executed by firing squad, he died with arms outstretched, crying 'Viva Cristo Rey!'

o.a: Saint Clement Striking the Rock by Bernardino Fungai, about 1500. Exiled to the Crimean mines, legend says, Clement saw a lamb on a hill and struck the rock there, and water gushed out for the thirsty prisoners. It is in the York Art Gallery.
o.b: The fourth Bishop of Rome, who may have known Peter and Paul. His letter to the quarreling church at Corinth is one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament.
o.t: Saint Clement I, Pope and Martyr

o.a: A fresco in the hermitage of San Colombano at Trambileno, Trentino, a tiny chapel built into a cliff face above a gorge. It is one of many places across Europe named for the wandering Irish monk.
o.b: An Irish monk who founded monasteries across France and Italy, from Luxeuil to Bobbio, carrying Irish learning to the continent.

o.a: Father Miguel Pro on the day of his arrest in 1927, in the civilian clothes he wore to minister in secret. The government photographed his execution to deter others; instead the pictures made him a hero.
o.b: A Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during the persecution of the Church. Executed by firing squad, he died with arms outstretched, crying 'Viva Cristo Rey!'
o.t: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro, Priest and Martyr

2027-11-23.t: Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro, Priest and Martyr

w.a: The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans under the Command of Titus, A.D. 70 by David Roberts, 1850. From the Mount of Olives the Roman army looks across at the burning city and its Temple.
w.b: “As for these things which you see, the days will come when there shall not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.”
w.t: Tuesday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-24.a: A Vietnamese painting from the mid-1800s showing the execution of Paul Mi, Peter Duong and Peter Truat on December 18, 1838. Pictures like this were made at the time to record the martyrs, and some were carried back to Paris by missionaries.
2027-11-24.b: A Vietnamese priest who gave his life with 116 companions—priests, catechists and lay people—during waves of persecution in Vietnam. They were canonized together in 1988.
2027-11-24.t: Saint Andrew Dũng-Lạc, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs

2027-11-25.a: Thanksgiving at Plymouth by Jennie Augusta Brownscombe, 1925, her second version of a scene she first painted in 1914. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington.
2027-11-25.b: A national day of gratitude to God for the harvest and the blessings of the year, kept on the fourth Thursday of November.

o.a: Saint Catherine of Alexandria by Caravaggio, about 1598, painted for his patron Cardinal del Monte. She kneels beside the broken spiked wheel, a sword in her hand. His model was a Roman courtesan, Fillide Melandroni. It is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
o.b: According to legend, a learned young noblewoman of Alexandria who out-argued the emperor's philosophers and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered, she was beheaded.
o.t: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Virgin and Martyr

o.a: Thanksgiving at Plymouth by Jennie Augusta Brownscombe, 1925, her second version of a scene she first painted in 1914. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington.
o.b: A national day of gratitude to God for the harvest and the blessings of the year, kept on the fourth Thursday of November.

w.a: The Destruction of the Temple of Jerusalem by Francesco Hayez, 1867. Roman soldiers storm the Temple in AD 70 as the city burns, the fall Jesus foretold. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
w.b: “And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.”
w.t: Thursday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-26.a: The Great Day of His Wrath by John Martin, 1851–53, the first of three vast paintings of the Last Judgment. Mountains collapse and a city tumbles into the abyss — 'heaven and earth will pass away.' It is in Tate Britain, London.
2027-11-26.b: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.”
2027-11-26.t: Friday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-27.a: The Last Judgment by Rogier van der Weyden, 1445–50, painted for the hospital of Beaune in Burgundy so that the sick could see it from their beds. St. Michael weighs souls beneath Christ in judgment. It is still in the Hôtel-Dieu, Beaune.
2027-11-27.b: “But watch at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that will take place, and to stand before the Son of man.”
2027-11-27.t: Saturday of the thirty-fourth week of Ordinary Time

2027-11-28.a: The Last Judgment by Michelangelo, 1536–41, covering the whole altar wall of the Sistine Chapel. Christ raises his arm in judgment as the dead rise and the saints crowd around him; it took Michelangelo five years.
2027-11-28.b: “Now when these things begin to take place, look up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”

2027-11-29.a: Christ and the Centurion by Paolo Veronese, about 1571. The Roman officer kneels in armor before Christ, his soldiers around him, in a Venetian street. It is in the Prado Museum, Madrid.
2027-11-29.b: “Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.”
2027-11-29.t: Monday of the first week of Advent

2027-11-30.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Andrew by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, painted in Seville around 1675–82. Andrew is bound to the X-shaped cross that became his emblem, as light breaks through the clouds above. It hangs in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.
2027-11-30.b: A fisherman of Galilee and brother of Peter, he was the first apostle Jesus called. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross in Greece; he is patron of Scotland.

2027-12-01.a: The Miracle of the Loaves and Fishes by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, 1670–74, painted for the church of the Hospital de la Caridad in Seville, a brotherhood that fed the poor. It still hangs there.
2027-12-01.b: “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have been with me now three days, and have nothing to eat; and I am unwilling to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the way.”
2027-12-01.t: Wednesday of the first week of Advent

2027-12-02.a: The House Built on Rock, an engraving after Hendrick Goltzius, the great Dutch engraver of the late 1500s. The wise man's house stands firm on rock while the storm rages. It is in the North Holland Archives, Haarlem.
2027-12-02.b: “Not every one who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.”
2027-12-02.t: Thursday of the first week of Advent

2027-12-03.a: The famous Japanese portrait of Francis Xavier, painted in the early 1600s and found in 1920, hidden in the home of a family of secret Christians near Osaka. He gazes up at the cross, his heart aflame. It is in the Kobe City Museum.
2027-12-03.b: One of St. Ignatius's first companions, he sailed for Asia and preached the Gospel in India, Malaysia and Japan. He died on an island off the coast of China and is patron of missions.

2027-12-04.a: Saint John of Damascus in a 14th or 15th-century fresco on Mount Athos. He wears the turban he would have worn as an official at the Caliph's court in Damascus, before he became a monk.
2027-12-04.b: A monk near Jerusalem who defended the veneration of holy images during the iconoclast controversy. A Doctor of the Church.

o.a: Saint John of Damascus in a 14th or 15th-century fresco on Mount Athos. He wears the turban he would have worn as an official at the Caliph's court in Damascus, before he became a monk.
o.b: A monk near Jerusalem who defended the veneration of holy images during the iconoclast controversy. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint John Damascene, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-12-04.t: Saint John Damascene, Priest and Doctor of the Church

w.a: The Harvesters by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1565, one of his series of the months. 'The harvest is abundant': peasants cut and stack golden wheat and rest at noon under a pear tree. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
w.b: “When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.”
w.t: Saturday of the first week of Advent

2027-12-05.a: Saint John the Baptist by Titian, about 1540, a powerful figure of the prophet in the wilderness with his lamb beside him. It is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
2027-12-05.b: “All flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

2027-12-06.a: Saint Nicholas Saves Three Innocents from Death by Ilya Repin, 1888. The bishop seizes the executioner's sword just before it falls. It is in the State Russian Museum, St. Petersburg.
2027-12-06.b: Bishop of Myra, famed for secret gifts to the poor—the origin of Santa Claus. He is patron of children, sailors and Russia.

o.a: Saint Nicholas Saves Three Innocents from Death by Ilya Repin, 1888. The bishop seizes the executioner's sword just before it falls. It is in the State Russian Museum, St. Petersburg.
o.b: Bishop of Myra, famed for secret gifts to the poor—the origin of Santa Claus. He is patron of children, sailors and Russia.

w.a: Christ Healing the Paralytic, a wall painting from the house-church at Dura-Europos in Syria, about AD 232, one of the oldest known pictures of Christ. The healed man walks away carrying his bed. It is in the Yale University Art Gallery.
w.b: “I say to you, rise, take up your bed and go home.”
w.t: Monday of the second week of Advent

2027-12-07.a: A detail of the polyptych of Saint Ambrose by Giovanni Barbagelata, 1499, still in the parish church of Sant'Ambrogio in Varazze on the Ligurian coast. Ambrose is shown in bishop's robes, with the scourge he used against heresy.
2027-12-07.b: A Roman governor who was acclaimed Bishop of Milan by the people before he was even baptized. A great preacher and hymn-writer, he stood up to emperors and baptized St. Augustine.
2027-12-07.t: Saint Ambrose, Bishop and Doctor of the Church

2027-12-08.a: The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables by Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, about 1678. Looted from Seville by Napoleon's Marshal Soult, it was bought by the Louvre in 1852 for the highest price ever paid for a painting, and returned to Spain in 1941. It is in the Museo del Prado.
2027-12-08.b: The Church celebrates that Mary, by a singular grace, was preserved from all stain of original sin from the first moment of her conception. Patronal feast of the United States.
2027-12-08.t: The Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

2027-12-09.a: Saint Juan Diego with the Tilma, a Mexican painting of 1737. He opens his cloak to show the roses he gathered in December, and the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on the cloth.
2027-12-09.b: An Indigenous Mexican to whom the Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak: Our Lady of Guadalupe.

o.a: Saint Juan Diego with the Tilma, a Mexican painting of 1737. He opens his cloak to show the roses he gathered in December, and the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe on the cloth.
o.b: An Indigenous Mexican to whom the Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak: Our Lady of Guadalupe.

w.a: Saint John the Baptist in the Wilderness by Caravaggio, about 1604. The prophet sits alone in the dark, wrapped in a red cloak, his reed cross beside him. It is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.
w.b: “Truly, I say to you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist.”
w.t: Thursday of the second week of Advent

2027-12-10.a: The Madonna of Loreto by Domenico Fiasella, about 1643. Angels carry the Holy House of Nazareth through the air to Loreto, as the legend tells. It is in the Diocesan Museum, Genoa.
2027-12-10.b: The Holy House of Loreto, venerated as the home of the Holy Family at Nazareth, has drawn pilgrims for centuries. Our Lady of Loreto is patron of aviators.

o.a: The Madonna of Loreto by Domenico Fiasella, about 1643. Angels carry the Holy House of Nazareth through the air to Loreto, as the legend tells. It is in the Diocesan Museum, Genoa.
o.b: The Holy House of Loreto, venerated as the home of the Holy Family at Nazareth, has drawn pilgrims for centuries. Our Lady of Loreto is patron of aviators.

w.a: Children's Games by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1560. A whole town square is taken over by children playing some eighty different games, like the children in the market place Jesus describes. It is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
w.b: “We piped to you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.”
w.t: Friday of the second week of Advent

2027-12-11.a: Saint Damasus, a 16th-century Portuguese panel by an unknown painter, in the Alberto Sampaio Museum in Guimarães—the city that claims him as a native son.
2027-12-11.b: Pope who commissioned St. Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin, the Vulgate. He honored the martyrs by restoring the catacombs and writing verses for their tombs.

o.a: Saint Damasus, a 16th-century Portuguese panel by an unknown painter, in the Alberto Sampaio Museum in Guimarães—the city that claims him as a native son.
o.b: Pope who commissioned St. Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin, the Vulgate. He honored the martyrs by restoring the catacombs and writing verses for their tombs.

w.a: Elijah in the Desert by Washington Allston, 1818. The prophet kneels in a barren landscape as the ravens bring him food. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
w.b: “But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not know him, but did to him whatever they pleased.”
w.t: Saturday of the second week of Advent

2027-12-12.a: The Preaching of Saint John the Baptist by Rembrandt, about 1634–35, painted in shades of brown as a study. A great crowd of every kind of listener, some rapt, some bored, gathers around the prophet. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-12-12.b: “I baptize you with water; but he who is mightier than I is coming, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.”

2027-12-13.a: The Burial of Saint Lucy by Caravaggio, 1608, painted in Syracuse while he was on the run. Two huge gravediggers dwarf the mourners around her body. It was painted for the church of Santa Lucia al Sepolcro, built over the place of her burial.
2027-12-13.b: A young Christian of Sicily who gave her dowry to the poor and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means 'light', and her feast falls in the darkest days of the year.

2027-12-14.a: Christ Crucified with a Carmelite friar, probably John of the Cross, attributed to Agustín del Castillo, early 1600s. John's own small drawing of Christ on the cross, seen from above, later inspired Salvador Dalí. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts of Córdoba.
2027-12-14.b: A Carmelite friar who worked with St. Teresa of Ávila to reform the order. His poems, including The Dark Night, are among the treasures of Spanish literature. A Doctor of the Church.
2027-12-14.t: Saint John of the Cross, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-12-15.a: Saint John the Baptist in Prison Visited by Two Disciples by Giovanni di Paolo, 1455–60, one of a series of panels on John's life. John sends his disciples through the barred window to ask, 'Are you the one who is to come?' It is in the Art Institute of Chicago.
2027-12-15.b: “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good news preached to them.”
2027-12-15.t: Wednesday of the third week of Advent

2027-12-16.a: The Appearance of Christ Before the People by Alexander Ivanov, 1837–57, a canvas more than seven meters wide that took him twenty years. John the Baptist points to the distant figure of Christ: 'Prepare the way of the Lord.' It is in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
2027-12-16.b: “I tell you, among those born of women none is greater than John; yet he who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
2027-12-16.t: Thursday of the third week of Advent

2027-12-17.a: The Tree of Jesse, about 1500, from the circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans in Haarlem. The kings of Israel sit in the branches of a tree growing from the sleeping Jesse, with the Virgin and Child at the top. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-12-17.b: “Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.”
2027-12-17.by: Circle of Geertgen tot Sint Jans

2027-12-18.a: The Dream of Saint Joseph by Georges de La Tour, about 1640. By the light of a single candle, a child-like angel touches the sleeping Joseph's arm. It is in the Museum of Arts, Nantes.
2027-12-18.b: “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.”

2027-12-19.a: The Visitation by Jacopo Pontormo, about 1528–29. Mary and Elizabeth embrace in a swirl of brilliant color, watched by two women who seem to be their own doubles. It is in the church of San Michele at Carmignano, near Florence.
2027-12-19.b: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!”

2027-12-20.a: The Annunciation by Jan van Eyck, about 1434–36. Gabriel greets Mary in a dim Romanesque church, and their words are written in gold between them; Mary's answer is painted upside down so that God can read it. It is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
2027-12-20.b: “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.”

2027-12-21.a: The Visitation by Rogier van der Weyden, about 1435–40. Mary and Elizabeth, both expecting, meet on a path in the Flemish countryside, each resting a hand on the other. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Leipzig.
2027-12-21.b: “Blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfilment of what was spoken to her from the Lord.”
2027-12-21.m: Commemoration of Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church

o.a: Saint Peter Canisius, an anonymous portrait. The Dutch Jesuit's catechisms went through hundreds of editions in his lifetime and he was called the second apostle of Germany.
o.b: A Dutch Jesuit whose catechisms renewed Catholic life in Germany after the Reformation. A Doctor of the Church.
o.t: Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church

2027-12-22.a: The Madonna of the Magnificat by Sandro Botticelli, about 1483. Mary writes the words of her song in a book held by angels, while the Child guides her hand. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
2027-12-22.b: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden. For behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.”

2027-12-23.a: The Naming of John the Baptist by Fra Angelico, about 1435. Zechariah, still unable to speak, writes 'His name is John' while Elizabeth's household looks on. It is in the Museo di San Marco, Florence.
2027-12-23.b: “He asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, ‘His name is John.’ And they all marveled.”
2027-12-23.m: Commemoration of Saint John of Kanty, Priest

o.a: A Miracle of Saint John of Kanty by Taddeo Kuntze, about 1767. The Kraków professor was known for giving away his own clothes and food to the poor. It is in the National Museum in Kraków.
o.b: A professor at the University of Kraków, known for his learning and his great generosity to the poor.

2027-12-24.a: The Angel Appearing to the Shepherds by Thomas Cole, 1833–34, founder of the Hudson River School. The angel's light breaks over a vast moonlit landscape. It is in the Chrysler Museum of Art, Norfolk, Virginia.
2027-12-24.b: “Through the tender mercy of our God, when the day shall dawn upon us from on high to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

2027-12-25.a: The Adoration of the Child by Gerard van Honthorst, about 1620. All the light comes from the baby. Badly damaged by a car bomb outside the Uffizi in 1993, it was restored and hangs again in the Uffizi, Florence.
2027-12-25.b: Christmas: the Son of God is born of the Virgin Mary in a stable at Bethlehem and laid in a manger, while angels sing to shepherds in the fields.

2027-12-26.a: The Doni Tondo by Michelangelo, about 1506, his only finished panel painting. It was made for the wedding of Agnolo Doni in Florence. The Child passes between Mary and Joseph, with nude youths behind and the infant John the Baptist. It is in the Uffizi, still in its original carved frame.
2027-12-26.b: A feast of the home at Nazareth, where Jesus grew 'in wisdom and age and grace' with Mary and Joseph. It is kept in the octave of Christmas as a model for every family.
2027-12-26.t: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph

2027-12-27.a: Saint John on Patmos by Hieronymus Bosch, about 1489. John gazes at a vision of the Woman clothed with the sun while a little devil tries to steal his ink. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
2027-12-27.b: The beloved disciple, who leaned on Jesus at the Last Supper and stood at the foot of the cross. The Gospel, letters and Revelation are attributed to him.

2027-12-28.a: The Massacre of the Innocents by Peter Paul Rubens, about 1638, one of two he painted of the subject. Mothers fight Herod's soldiers for their children as cherubs bring the martyrs' crowns from above. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.
2027-12-28.b: The little boys of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. They are honored as the first to die for him.

2027-12-29.a: Simeon's Song of Praise by Rembrandt, 1631. In a vast, dim temple one shaft of light falls on old Simeon holding the Child, with Mary and Joseph kneeling beside him. It is in the Mauritshuis, The Hague.
2027-12-29.b: “Lord, now let your servant depart in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to your people Israel.”
2027-12-29.m: Commemoration of Saint Thomas Becket, Bishop and Martyr

o.a: The Martyrdom of Saint Thomas Becket by Jean-Baptiste Marie Pierre, 1748. The king's knights strike down the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral. It is in the church of Notre-Dame-de-la-Nativité de Bercy, Paris.
o.b: Archbishop of Canterbury and former chancellor to King Henry II, murdered in his cathedral for defending the freedom of the Church.
o.t: Saint Thomas Becket, Bishop and Martyr

2027-12-29.t: Fifth Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord

2027-12-30.a: An Old Woman Reading, probably the Prophetess Anna, by Rembrandt, 1631. Light falls on the old woman's hand resting on the page of Scripture. It is in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
2027-12-30.b: “Coming up at that very hour she gave thanks to God, and spoke of him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.”
2027-12-30.t: Sixth Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord

2027-12-31.a: The Holy Night by Correggio, about 1528–30, one of the first paintings in which all the light comes from the newborn Child. It is in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
2027-12-31.b: “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth; we have beheld his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father.”
2027-12-31.m: Commemoration of Saint Sylvester I, Pope

o.a: The Legend of Saint Sylvester by Agnolo Gaddi, about 1380–85. Legend tells how the pope tamed a dragon that was poisoning Rome. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
o.b: Pope during the reign of Constantine, when the Church emerged from persecution. In his time the first great basilicas of Rome were built and the Council of Nicaea was held.

2027-12-31.t: Seventh Day within the Octave of the Nativity of the Lord
